The measurement results show that the 4-bit SiC flash ADC can operate reliably up to at least 200 degrees Celsius, which outperforms the Si counterpart regarding the maximum operating temperature.

articleTitle: HeartRhythm: ECG-Based Music Preference Classification in Popular Music
abstract: Electrocardiogram (ECG) is a promising signal for music psychology research, but it is rare to find a music study applying ECG to machine learning, especially in music preference tasks. This study conducts an ECG-based music preference classification (favored vs. non-favored). The model is evaluated on a MUSEC dataset providing ECG data from 20 humans listening to two types of music: music without (Melody) and with (Song) lyrics. We also investigate the efficiency of physiological and statistical features and compare the model efficiency of ECG with the electroencephalography (EEG) studies listening to the same songs. Our results reveal that the random forest algorithm with statistical features indicates the outstanding F1-scores in Melody and Song <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(82.95 \pm 7.92\%$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$84.13 \pm 5.14\%$</tex>, respectively). Moreover, the models can outperform the EEG studies. The result opens the opportunity of using ML with ECG to provide a better experience in appreciating music.

articleTitle: Non-Contact Lamb Wave Defect Detection Based Solely on Air-Coupled Ultrasonic Phased Arrays
abstract: Air-coupled ultrasonic non-destructive testing (NDT) enables the inspection of composite materials for defects. In this paper, we investigate non-contact defect detection based on Lamb waves by using two dedicated air-coupled ultrasonic phased arrays, i.e. one for transmission and one for reception. The major challenge is the signal detection of the reflected leaky Lamb wave originating from the defect, despite a strong interfering signal, i.e. the direct air-path wave, causing a so-called blind zone. Therefore, we exploit the angular difference of the reflected leaky Lamb wave and the direct air-path wave by applying high-resolution direction of arrival <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{DoA})$</tex> estimation algorithms, i.e. MVDR beamformer (Capon) and MUSIC algorithms, as well as image deconvolution methods, i.e. CLEAN and Richardson-Lucy algorithms. First, we assess the signal detection capability by using Monte Carlo simulations considering realistic non-ideal array elements. Second, we validate the simulations by conducting testbed measurements, which show that conventional beamforming (CBF), MVDR and MUSIC are capable of fully air-coupled defect detection, even when the direct air-path wave is impinging. We conclude that the blind zone can be eliminated and show that the MUSIC algorithm excels in highlighting the reflected leaky Lamb wave.

articleTitle: Reduced Graphene Oxide-Based Chemiresistive NO2sensor: Metal Oxide Nanoparticles Decoration Effect
abstract: We present the development of a stretchable platform-based nitrogen dioxide (NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) gas sensor that operates at room temperature (RT). This study investigates the impact of incorporating metal oxide nanoparticles (NPs) into a chemiresistive NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gas sensor, utilizing reduced graphene oxide (rGO) as the primary sensing material. By introducing mesoporous ZnFe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> (ZFO) NPs at different concentrations into the rGO sensing layer, the performance of the gas sensor is significantly enhanced. The inclusion of ZFO NPs, which possess high-density defect sites, contributes to fast response and recovery times across a wide range of NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>concentrations (150 to 4000 ppb). Various transient parameters are analyzed to assess the effects of ZFO NPs integration. The rGO-ZFO-based gas sensor exhibits improved sensitivity and reproducibility. Moreover, these sensors, integrated into a stretchable platform and capable of RT operation, open possibilities for the development of advanced wearable NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gas sensors in the future.

articleTitle: Capacitive Sensor for Flame Detection in Pipes
abstract: In the recent years, ensuring the safety and reliability of industrial processes has become an increasingly critical challenge. The flame detection in pipes remains a crucial area of concern. We propose an innovative approach utilizing a capacitive sensor for flame detection in pipes. The sensor harnesses the electrical properties of flames offering a promising alternative to traditional detection methods. The design focuses on maximizing the sensitivity considering parasitic capacitances of the assembly. Following the trend in the industry towards digitization and miniaturization, an integrated capacitance to digital converter is used, combining a superb accuracy and a high sample rate. The capacitive sensor demonstrates high effectiveness in detecting flames at a test facility.

articleTitle: Ultrasonic Sensor for Pipe Joint Make-up Assessment
abstract: Reliable leakage-free facilities, cost-reasonable handling and ease of deployment are extremely important factors for hydrocarbons casing and tubing make-up. In this paper, we propose a novel technique to assess the tightness of pipe joints make-up assessment from ultrasonic sensors. A system based on piezoelectric transducers and a performant electronic device is used to detect the metal-to-metal sealing. The proposed method, performing wideband impedance analysis of an accessible piezoelectric transducer, allows the measurement, across a thick metal barrier, of the state of an inaccessible on/off sensor. The extreme simplicity of the proposed technology opens new opportunities in the field of acoustic communication through metal wall

articleTitle: A Multi-Surface Acoustic Wave Sensor Platform for the Detection and Identification of Toxic Gases
abstract: In this paper, we present a platform based on a modular approach coupled with powerful algorithms for accurate detection and identification of chemical compounds. The system relies on multi-SAW (Surface Acoustic Wave) sensors that are functionalized differently, resulting in multi-responses that collectively constitute a fingerprint of the chemical compound. A prototype has been developed and the overall system, including the design of SAW module, the acquisition system, learning algorithms and online recognition of various compounds, has been tested and validated. The results showed a reliable and accurate system with a perfect score of 100% recognition of DMMP.

articleTitle: Continuous Measurement of Individual Formaldehyde Exposure with a DIY Photometer
abstract: Formaldehyde is widely used in pathology for the preservation of tissue specimens. Due to a lack of alternatives, it continues to be used despite its toxic properties. Currently existing sensors are not suitable for daily use in pathology due to their long reaction times in the range of minutes (electrochemical) or the size of their volume of more than 5 liters (optical). In order to accurately record the individual exposure of employees and thus enable targeted protective measures, a mobile formaldehyde sensor based on a 340 nm UV-LED is presented. To enhance the absorption in a compact design, a multi-pass cell is developed that extends the light-gas interaction by mirroring the light. With the developed photometer, it is possible to measure formaldehyde concentrations down to a minimum of 2 ppm at an averaging period of 1 s. The limiting factor to further decrease the lowest measurement limit of the photometer is the light loss in the multi-pass cell due to beam expansion and absorption by the mirrors. Possibilities to reduce the light loss are shown in order to monitor the permissible individual exposure at work of 0.3 ppm.

articleTitle: Exploring the Potential of Magnetically Active Polymers in Force Sensing: Material, Design, and Experimental Insights
abstract: In our study, we delve into the potential of magnetically active polymers as base material for soft force sensors. The novelty of the approach lies in this elastomer's dual role as a permanent magnet and soft interface which upon deformation exhibits a change in remanent magnetic field. We tested three distinct formulations, each permanently magnetized through their thickness and proceeded to characterize these variants mechanically, magnetically, and thermally, before shaping them into a hollow ring geometry mounted on a PCB with hall sensor for our force sensing purposes. We performed cyclic and stepwise loading compression tests up to 100 N on the produced sensor and observed a linear increase in remanent magnetic field with sensitivities of up to 9 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{T}/\mathrm{N}$</tex>. In addition, the temperature cycling tests of up to 75°C highlighted a constrained decrease of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$< 7\%$</tex> of the initial remanent magnetic field. Combined with measured hardnesses spanning from 60 ShA to 70 ShA and densities <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$< 2\mathrm{g}/\text{cm}3$</tex>, these elastomers show promise of mass manufacturable, low cost and compact force sensors for various contact applications.

articleTitle: A Gas Imaging Sensor System of Automotive Exhaust Plumes for Remote Emission Sensing Application Basing on Schlieren Imaging An Approach to Visualize and Size Vehicle Exhaust Plumes
abstract: In this work we present a system for remote emission sensing (RES), focusing on a system for optical gas imaging, to enable direct concentration measurements by a Tunable Diode Laser Absorption Spectroscopy (TDLAS) technique. The technique is basing on background oriented schlieren imaging to give a robust information of the exhaust plume size, thus the absorption length of the laser. We present the description of the system, our approach of AI-based image processing and verification results. The gas imaging system was tested on-road and characterized in lab with controlled gas mixtures. First results from lab characterization and on-road measurements prove the feasibility of the approach, i.e. exhaust plumes of passing cars are reliably detected and the sizes of plumes are then calculated appropriately.

articleTitle: Adaptive 3-Mode Thermal Flow and Velocity Sensor
abstract: A fully programmed, adaptive flow sensor system has been designed, simulated, manufactured and tested. A 3-mode drive and read-out method is proposed consisting of anemometric, calorimetric and transition regions. The adaptive flow sensor system choses the best drive/read-out method based on flow rate and uses this to calculate predicted flow rate. This 3-mode method results in a bi-directional flow sensing system that is extremely accurate (~0.1 sccm) enabling low flow measurements whilst maintaining a large range (-250 sccm to 250 sccm). Additionally, the transition mode is essential for smoothing and allowing a calibratable response. A population of 24 calibrated devices with adaptive 3-mode functionality have been presented and shown to predict flow across a large range of flow rates (-250 sccm - 250 sccm) and ambient temperatures (-30°C - 85°C). This has demonstrated a miniature, cheap, highly accurate, low power-consumption and wide-range flow sensing system that can be used for a multitude of applications

articleTitle: High-Precision Time-Frequency Synchronization for Mobile Distributed Coherent Systems
abstract: Distributed coherent systems can achieve high signal-to-noise ratio gain through close collaboration among multiple nodes. High-precision time-frequency synchronization between nodes is one of the main challenges to realize distributed coherence on small-scale mobile platforms, such as vehicles and drones. This paper proposes a time-frequency synchronization method based on a pulse time division system, which can achieve phase-level precision on mobile platforms. The effectiveness of the proposed method was verified through a ground vehicle experiment. The root mean square of synchronization errors was 34.49ps, while the short-term frequency stability reached <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.86\times 10^{=12}$</tex> @1s.

articleTitle: Independently Operational Dual-Frequency Band Metamaterial Based EM Biosensor for Identification and Quantification of Impurities in Vegetable Oils
abstract: In this paper, a highly sensitive electromagnetic (EM) biosensor has been designed and demonstrated, showing its utility in determining the inorganic impurity in vegetable oils. Firstly, the modified split ring resonator is designed to generate a dual-frequency band, and by applying anti-symmetry phenomena, those frequency bands are made independent to explicitly detect the resonance frequencies for inorganic and organic compounds (vegetable oils). Further, different vegetable oil specimens are placed at the top of the resonator, and depending upon the presence of an inorganic impurity, a change in the resonance behaviour is observed. Finally, a thorough analysis has been performed, and the prototype is fabricated, followed by realistic measurement in terms of impurity identification and estimation that shows its applicability in the food industry.

articleTitle: Estimation of Splitting Interval in Second Heart Sound by Optimizing a Demixing Vector
abstract: A non-invasive method to estimate the splitting interval (SI) of the second heart sound (S2) was developed and evaluated. Recently, there has been a growing need for a non-invasive SI estimation for the early detection of cardiovascular diseases. Therefore, we proposed an SI estimation algorithm by separating the aortic and pulmonary components (A2 and P2, respectively) from S2 with an optimized demixing vector and mathematical model of S2. Herein, we evaluated the SI estimation performance of our algorithm. As a result, our algorithm could determine a simulated S2's SI with an error of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.3+1.0$</tex> ms. A2 and P2 were separated from recorded human S2 signals. The resulting SI estimation of the recorded data showed a correlation coefficient with S2-S2 intervals of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r=- 0.67$</tex>. This negative correlation is consistent with reported physiological features of the heart.

articleTitle: Low-Cost Chipless RFID Glucose Sensor for Diabetes Screening
abstract: Diabetes is a widely spread chronic metabolic dis-ease that in many cases goes undiagnosed, especially in developing countries. In this paper, we present the design, implementation and testing of a low-cost, small-size chipless RFID sensor integrated with a glucose-Concavalin A affinity based sensitive fluid. The sensor is capable of measuring physiological blood glucose levels as a function of the flow rate of a mixture of the sensitive material and blood plasma through a paper channel. Experiments have been conducted to ensure that the sensor is able to differentiate between high and low plasma glucose concentrations (2.5 mM and 10 mM). The obtained results are statistically significant and prove that the sensor can be an option for mass screenings especially in medium- and low-income countries where access to regular medical equipment is limited.

articleTitle: Magnetic Imaging of Thimble Tube Using Integrated Array TMR Sensors
abstract: To avoid safety accidents and economic losses, the structure health of the thimble tube that provides a guide and channel for the neutron flux measurement probe in a nuclear reactor core should be evaluated periodically. It is difficult for the current probe based on an induction coil to quantify the defects. This paper presents a probe with array tunnel magnetoresistance (TMR) sensors, which are integrated into a circular printed circuit board (PCB) with a 4.8 mm diameter. It can obtain a magnetic field image in a probe pass. The defect depth and circumferential length are estimated by analyzing the image, based on which the safety state of the thimble tube can be quantitatively assessed.

articleTitle: Current Developments and Future Directions in Using IMUs for Injury Prevention in Running
abstract: Running is a popular activity that contributes to better physical and mental health. Running is, however, associated with high numbers of running related injuries (RRI) [1]. The etiology of these injuries is assumed to be multifactorial but still not fully clear. A recent systematic review showed that training load management and kinematic and kinetic factors are associated with RRIs, but few direct causal relations were found [2]. It is assumed that accumulating fatigue also plays an important role, negatively impacting the preferred movement pattern of a runner, leading to overload [3]. The main reason that the etiology of RRIs is still unclear is that most studies have been performed in the standardized and controlled gait laboratory. The limited measurement volume and/or the cyclical nature of the treadmill are not representative of the setting where people typically run and get injured. Therefore, experiments need to be performed in the real world to get a better understanding of running RRIs to eventually prevent them. Inertial magnetic measurement units (IMUs) allow for three dimensional assessment of (changes in) running technique in the sport specific setting.

articleTitle: Demonstration of a Wide Range Conductivity Sensor for Buffers on-Demand Manufacturing
abstract: The aim of this work is to show the feasibility of an on-chip conductivity sensor for quality control during buffer preparation in biomanufacturing, using solutions with different chemical compositions. To optimize the sensor accuracy across a broad conductivity range (0.05 to 180 mS/cm), we selected a microfabricated four-electrode sensor and employed multi-point calibration to determine its apparent cell constant. Impedance spectra were captured (80 Hz to 80 kHz), followed by data post-processing to select resistive frequency bands based on the measured impedance phase angle. This study demonstrates sensor stability over 45 days in six solutions commonly used in buffer manufacturing processes and its compatibility with sanitization processes such as clean-in-place (CIP), and steam-in-place (SIP). Across all experiments, the sensor consistently showed a relative error below 5% compared to a commercial sensor in static and dynamic conditions. The performance of the presented sensor, using the multi-point calibration, establishes it as a reliable tool for quality control in cost-effective, on-demand buffer manufacturing.

articleTitle: Two-dimensional Passive Type Micro Mixer using Dean flow and Asymmetric Channel Structure
abstract: This paper is a study on a two-dimensional passive type mixer of a new shape. The proposed mixer is configured with a curved channel to use the Dean flow. And the curved channel is divided into two channels of different widths. Fluids were mixed more quickly using this structure, and this two-dimensional passive type mixer was easily and economically manufactured using soft lithography. We verified the mixing efficiency of the mixer by changing various factors such as the channel separation ratio and the shape of the curve.

articleTitle: A CMOS-MEMS Pressure Sensor with Integrated Front-End for Chemical Vapor Deposition Systems
abstract: In this paper, a CMOS-MEMS capacitive pressure sensor is designed for low-pressure chemical vapor deposition (LPCVD) systems. A buffer layer is utilized in the proposed pressure transducer to effectively protect the sensing diaphragm from breaking down while maintaining high linearity with a compact dimension. A low-power front-end readout circuit is implemented on the same chip to convert the capacitance variance to digital outputs according to the pressure change in the chemical vapor deposition process, near vacuum in this design. The presented device is fabricated through UMC 0.18μm 1P6M CMOS process, and in-house post-processes. The chip size is 1.5×1.5 mm2. Experimental results show that the sensitivity of 0.655 fF/Pa is realized in the range of 0 – 600 Pa.

articleTitle: Sensor Inserts on Spherical Surfaces for Temperature Measurement in Wear Contacts
abstract: Wear and the resulting temperature has a significant influence on the frictional contact behavior of two surfaces in contact. In order to establish accurate wear prediction models, it is essential to measure the temperature at the point of action. This work shows the approach for manufacturing a component-inherent temperature sensor on a ceramic sphere via laser structuring in order to measure friction-induced temperature changes precisely at the point of action during tribologically relevant ball-on-disc tests. Within this paper, different sensor layouts are tested and the sensor fabrication and high temperature contacting via laser direct structuring on ceramics is revealed in detail. A TCR of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2440\pm 123\ \text{ppm}/^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> could be achieved after an annealing process for the layout with the smallest line width. Measurements of the wear resistance of the Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> layer showed, that the sensors life span enables a sliding distance of at least 1,000 mm. During the tribological testing, friction induced temperature changes as well as short-term temperature peaks were measured.

articleTitle: Smart Fault Detection Approach Leveraging Soft Sensor and Model-Free Control: Application to Robot Manipulator
abstract: Fault detection and diagnosis (FDD) in smart manufacturing (SM) has become a significant area of research due to its potential impact on safety, robustness, and overall durability. This paper presents a novel Model-Free Fault Detection (MFFD) method inspired by the Model-Free Controller (MFC), addressing the limitations of existing FDD approaches. Unlike traditional data-driven and model-based methods, the MFFD method eliminates the dependence on physical laws and reduces the need for large datasets and extensive computational resources. The proposed method is based on fault estimation leveraging soft sensors to compare them with a reference signal obtained under normal conditions. The validation and effectiveness of the proposed MFFD method is demonstrated through simulation results on a SCARA robot, focusing on actuator faults.

articleTitle: Near-Zero-Power Passive Wireless Underground Soil Moisture Sensor
abstract: This paper presents the design and laboratory characterization of a near-zero-power passive wireless underground soil moisture sensor. The system employs two inductively coupled LC tank circuits operated under a two-phase operation with a time-domain resonant response-based sensing scheme to achieve a large sensing distance. A 40cm-diameter primary coil and 6cm-diameter secondary coil are designed to obtain high quality factors above 100 at high frequency over a typical soil moisture range. An operating frequency of 6MHz is chosen to maximize system sensitivity achieving a frequency shift of 150kHz for soil moisture ranging from 20% to 45%. The passive sensor can be operated wirelessly under a soil depth of 15cm, limited by the system feed-through signal.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Droplet Menisci Recognition for Digital Microfluidic Devices
abstract: This paper presents the application of machine learning techniques, specifically deep learning, to enhance the performance and reliability of electrowetting-on-dielectric (EWOD) digital microfluidic (DMF) devices. During droplet manipulation within an EWOD DMF device, the menisci of the droplets carry valuable information, including fluid properties, droplet size, position, and dynamics. Recognizing and analyzing these droplet menisci can provide insights into reaction kinetics and device defects, enabling reliable feedback control for improved device operation. To achieve reliable control of EWOD DMF devices, this study focuses on the recognition of droplet menisci using a deep learning approach. The U-Net model, a highly effective deep learning architecture for image segmentation tasks, is integrated into the present study. A convolutional neural network with the U-Net architecture is implemented, and image segmentation is performed to accurately identify droplet menisci. The network is trained using a diverse dataset containing images of droplet under various conditions. Model parameters are optimized to ensure high accuracy and robust performance. Experimental tests are conducted on images of droplets in different conditions, and the trained network successfully recognizes menisci with a model accuracy of 98 %.

articleTitle: An Android Based Portable Biosensor System for Cardiac Risk-Stratification by Detecting HFABP in Human Plasma
abstract: In this work, we demonstrate an android application-based portable biosensor system built on a field-effect based interdigitated micro-electrode biosensing chip fabricated over a low-cost PCB substrate. The whole system consists of a biosensor chip-simultaneously able to analyze three samples, a portable USB powered readout board and an android application oriented towards risk-stratification of human heart-health based on the concentrations of cardiac-specific early-release biomarker HFABP in plasma matrix. The electrical transduction is realized by a novel composite nanostructured material graphite-ZnO (GF-ZnO), synthesized using hydrothermal method. The biosensor is able to detect the target biomarker in a wide dynamic range of concentrations from fg/mL to ng/mL in very low sample volume (∼1 micro liters), and in a time-efficient manner, sample to result time being just 20 minutes. We believe that such a system has an immense potential for point-of-care applications in near future by extensive experimentation with the clinical samples and data analyses.

articleTitle: Microfluidic Nanospray Emitters with a Liquid Junction for Sensitive Bioanalyses
abstract: This work reports the fabrication and development of microfabricated, microfluidic nanospray emitters for sensitive bioanalyses using mass spectrometry (MS). The nanospray emitters demonstrated a stable performance at flow rates below 100 nL/min, with RSD of the base peak intensity less than 2 %, enabling reliable performance for a wide range of analytical applications. The main advantages of the proposed nanospray emitters are high ionization efficiency and sensitivity, suitability for mass production, and direct coupling with separation techniques via a liquid junction.

articleTitle: Automatic Camera-Based Advanced Slump Flow Testing for Improved Reliability
abstract: Manual methods used in assessing concrete properties often face significant drawbacks due to inherent inaccuracies and human errors regarding measurements and timing. To address this, this study introduces a novel automated camera-based system designed for conducting slump flow measurements, for improving the consistency and accuracy of assessing concrete flowability and its subsequent effect on compressive and flexural strength. By acquiring real-time data and reducing human intervention, it provides accurate tracking of concrete flow dynamics, standardized timings, and reduces error margins, thereby improving test reliability. Moreover, the proposed slump flow approximation function facilitates continuous time-based analysis of fresh concrete flow, potentially improving concrete property prediction.

articleTitle: High Sensitivity pH Sensor Based on Liquid Droplet Motion Over Hydrophobic Polymer
abstract: This work proposes self-powered pH monitoring by studying the interfacial surface charge modulation as liquid droplets move over a pre-charged hydrophobic CYTOP polymer surface. Due to the large negative charge of CYTOP in the friction sequence, it can be used to build liquid droplet-based pH-detecting devices. Typically, chemical sensors based on the interaction of water and PTFE have a restricted pH detection sensitivity of approximately -74 mV per pH of the water droplet unit. We demonstrate that using the proposed mechanism, the developed pH sensor reaches a sensitivity of roughly -80 mV per pH unit, which is higher than that of a PTFE-based pH sensor. In this work, pH 4 was found to be the essential threshold in the interaction of CYTOP and water droplets. The CYTOP surface exhibits positive polarity when the pH value is greater than 4, whereas the water droplet exhibits negative polarity when the pH value is less than 4. Furthermore, a pH sensor can be utilized in conjunction with a water droplet motion-based energy harvester. Also, it has been observed that Receiver Operating Characteristics (ROC) are different with diverse pH values. We show as a proof-of-concept that the pH of water droplets can be continually monitored using our polymer-based pH sensor. The developed pH sensor could eventually be utilized to measure the pH of the sweat in order to monitor health conditions.

articleTitle: Determining Vegetable Oil Composition Via Spectral Analysis of Faraday Rotation
abstract: In this contribution we propose a method to determine the composition of transparent liquids by determining its Verdet constant as a function of the wavelength within the visible spectrum. The method is exemplified by measurements containing various mixtures of sunflower and rapeseed oil. Preliminary findings suggest, that this method should provide a comparatively fast, inexpensive, and precise way to analyze liquids like vegetable oils non-destructively. This may be especially important to determine the concentration of certain contaminants.

articleTitle: Estimation of Analyte's Vertical Positions above the Surface of Nanocapacitor Array Biosensors
abstract: A novel method is proposed to estimate the vertical position of analytes above the surface of nanoelectrode array biosensors, which monitor the capacitance fluctuations caused by analytes in a microfluidic channel. The position estimation method, which takes advantage of accurate physics-based numerical simulations and simple analytical models, is tested on measurements of polystyrene nanoparticles (NPs) with an advanced high frequency impedance spectroscopy platform equipped with a new and optimized microfluidic chamber. The NP height estimation is directly validated on physics-based numerical simulations. In addition, it is indirectly confirmed by showing that numerical simulations with random NP positions (in agreement with the experimental height distribution) yield response distributions closely matching their measured counterpart.

articleTitle: Development of a Microfluidic Platform for High-Throughput Characterization of Multiple Biophysical Properties of Single-Cell Membranes
abstract: Single-cell membrane biophysical properties, which including membrane potential, membrane tension, and specific membrane capacitance, can serve as label-free indicators for assessing cell type and state. However, conventional tools limited in their throughput, such as patch clamping and AFM, impose constraints in single-cell membrane biophysical properties detection. The application of microfluidics in single-cell biophysical measurements allows for a convenient and efficient detection with the capability of multi-parameter analysis. In this paper, a microfluidic platform for high-throughput characterization of multiple biophysical properties of single-cell membranes was developed. Using this platform, we successfully measured the membrane relative potential, membrane tension, and specific membrane capacitance of single cells.

articleTitle: Metglas Based Multi-Modal Sensing Employing Magnetostrictive and Triboelectric Properties
abstract: This work presents the development and investigation of a mechanomagnetic sensor with Metglas as the active layer for potential multimodal sensing applications. Along with the conventional bulk magnetostrictive properties of Metglas, surface charge retention based triboelectricity is investigated for the first time. The pristine Metglas exhibits a unique switch in its triboelectric polarity and converts from a tribo-positive to tribo-negative on annealing at 500<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">○</sup> C. Two hybrid devices, consisting of PVDF/Metglas/PTFE and PVDF/annealed Metglas/glass layers, are fabricated to quantify the dual triboelectric/ magnetoelectric output characteristics of Metglas. The two devices generate a peak output voltage of 0.75 V and 1 V at 60 kPa pressure. Applying a DC magnetic field of 4 kOe in addition to the applied pressure results in a significant increase in output voltage to 2 V and 2.25 V, respectively. Additionally, the device can produce an output voltage of 0.48 V when a time-varying magnetic field of 0.4 Oe is applied at 49.9 kHz and lead to a magnetic field sensitivity of 1.2 V/Oe and a limit of detection of 0.01 Oe.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Expandable Microsphere Pressure Sensor for Arterial Pulse Wave Measurements
abstract: This study presents an evaluation of an expandable microsphere pressure sensor for pulse wave measurements. The sensor is designed for non-invasive and long-term monitoring, with a pressure-sensitive layer fabricated of compressible microspheres and elastic polydimethylsiloxane. The performance of the sensor is compared against a reference sensor, and the measured signals are analyzed visually and numerically to gain a better understanding of the sensor's applicability for quantitative arterial assessment. The characteristic features of the pulse wave are visually observable in the measured signals. The analysis results indicate that the microsphere pressure sensor presents the potential to evaluate physiological parameters such as heart rate or arterial stiffness.

articleTitle: Increasing Sensitivity of Magnetic Tactile Sensors by Optimizing Arrangement of PM Array
abstract: This study focuses on enhancing the sensitivity of magnetic tactile sensors by rearrangement of the magnetic circuit using a specialized permanent magnet structure, specifically the implementation of a Halbach array configuration strategically placing the permanent magnets to optimize the horizontal magnetic flux density of the sensing element, while concurrently minimizing interference from side magnetic circuits. By adopting this approach supported by finite element analyses, the sensitivity of tactile magnetic sensors is found to be significantly amplified, leading to enhanced accuracy and performance in various applications.

articleTitle: Ammonia Leakage Detection for Naval Transport First Step Towards on-Board Detection in Presence of Water Vapour
abstract: The influence of a constant relative humidity level (0, 15 and 35<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) during experiments in which a microwave resonator detects ammonia in air is shown in this paper. This work demonstrates the ability of the device presented to the target gas (between 100 and 500 ppm) qualitatively and quantitatively at the three relative humidity levels tested. It is shown that the sensitivity of the device depends not only on the concentration but also on the level of relative humidity. The sensitive material employed is a TiO2 super-substrate deposited on the microstrip resonator. The sensor consists of a trapezoidal spiral pattern designed to operate across a broad frequency range spanning from 2 to 8 GHz. The intrinsic advantages of microwave transduction facilitate the miniaturization of the device and enable measurements to be made at room temperature, since heating of the sensitive material is not required. These characteristics are well adapted to detection needs in the naval transport sector.

articleTitle: Development of a High-Sensitivity Printed Impedance Based Electrochemical Sensor for Detecting E. Coli
abstract: In this study, a flexible substrate was used to develop a flexible printed impedance-based electrochemical sensor for the detection of wound bacteria. Escherichia coli was detected since it is a common pathogen causing wound infection. The electrochemical sensor was fabricated by screen printing silver/silver chloride (Ag/AgCl) ink in a dentated spiral structure onto a polyimide (Kapton) substrate as working/reference electrodes, respectively. The electrochemical sensor was evaluated for its capability to detect extremely low concentrations of E. coli in defibrinated sheep's blood. The electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) analysis of the printed sensor demonstrated its capability to detect E. coli at detection levels as low as 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> colony forming units (CFU)/mL. Additionally, the sensor exhibited the capability to distinguish various levels of E. coli in the concentration range from 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup> CFU/mL.

articleTitle: Low Power Flexible Sensor for Ambient Light-based Blood Oxygen Saturation Measurement
abstract: This paper demonstrates a novel reflective mode ambient light-based blood oxygen saturation (SpO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) measurement sensor. To add flexibility the sensor is fabricated using plastic film patterning. This also makes the sensor light-weight and comfortable to wear. The sensor design is based on maximizing the capture of reflected red and green PPG (photoplethysmography) signals from skin under ambient light conditions. Using the reflected ref and green PPG signals the SpO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is measured. The sensor is tested on three participants and results show that the flexible sensor's measurements have an average deviation of 1.5% SpO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and a maximum deviation of 3% SpO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> from reference measurements under ambient light conditions. The sensor does not need any LED to be turned on for measurement, thus, making it a low power, non-invasive, continuous SpO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> monitoring options for wearables.

articleTitle: From Conventional Non-Conductive Foams to Soft Piezoresistive Pressure Sensors: A Low-Cost Approach to Large-Area Pressure-Mapping
abstract: This article presents a low-cost, and scalable method for synthesizing large sheets of functionalized foam for soft resistive pressure sensing that is compatible with any commercially available non-conductive foam. The process is illustrated by soaking Pu (Polyurethane) foam in a carbon-based polymeric mixture resulting in a functional foam with large pressure detection range up to 500 kPa, while retaining its deformability and recoverability after cyclic compression. The foam also shows unprecedentedly fast response time of ~120 ms. The foam was integrated in a wearable respiration sensor and in a large multitouch sensing mat that allows for precise data acquisition on the position and intensity of various simultaneous touches without the occurrence of ghost touches.

articleTitle: Sensor Fusion by Spatial Encoding for Autonomous Driving
abstract: Sensor fusion is critical to perception systems for task domains such as autonomous driving and robotics. Recently, the Transformer integrated with CNN has demonstrated high performance in sensor fusion for various perception tasks. In this work, we introduce a method for fusing data from camera and LiDAR. By employing Transformer modules at multiple resolutions, proposed method effectively combines local and global contextual relationships. The performance of the proposed method is validated by extensive experiments with two adversarial benchmarks with lengthy routes and high-density traffics. The proposed method outperforms previous approaches with the most challenging benchmarks, achieving significantly higher driving and infraction scores. Compared with TransFuser, it achieves 8% and 19% improvement in driving scores for the Longest6 and Town05 Long benchmarks, respectively.

articleTitle: Development of a Flexible Polyimide-Thermoplastic Polyurethane Based Triboelectric Nanogenerator for Energy Harvesting Applications
abstract: A flexible vertical contact-separation mode triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) was developed for energy harvesting applications using laser-textured polyimide (PI) film as a tribo-negative and thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) as a tribo-positive layer. Surface modification of PI film in terms of roughness was performed to increase charge storage capacity by laser texturing process using a carbon dioxide based laser source. Scanning electron microscopy and optical profilometry were performed to validate the surface modification and quantify the surface roughness of the laser-textured PI film. The electrodes for TENG were fabricated by screen printing Ag ink on a flexible TPU and surface-modified PI substrates for scavenging mechanical energy into electrical energy. The performance of the TENG device was demonstrated by investigating the open-circuit voltage <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{V}_{\text{oc}})$</tex>, short-circuit current <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{I}_{\text{sc}})$</tex> and instantaneous consumed power on the resistive loads. The TENG fabricated with laser-textured PI film demonstrated a higher Voc of approximately 20 V peak-to-peak (Vp-p) due to its higher surface roughness, while the TENG fabricated with untreated PI film generated a Voc of 12 Vp-p during the contact-separation cyclic test. In addition, the open-circuit voltage of the TENG was stabilized at 20 V with a short-circuit current of 18 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{A}$</tex>.

articleTitle: MEMS Pressure Sensor Based on Piezoresistive Effect of MoS2 Film
abstract: Molybdenum disulfide (MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) has excellent electrical and mechanical properties and can be used as sensors. 2D MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is commonly used in sensors and is poorly compatible with MEMS. This paper found that the deposited vertical nanosheets of layered disulfide clamps have excellent piezoresistive properties, which can be prepared in large areas. Its piezoresistive mechanism is attributed to the fact that the tension or compression of the substrate with the stress of the substrate causes an increase or decrease in the spacing of the MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanosheets between the layers, which results in a change in the resistance of the nanosheets between the layers. The piezoresistive factor of the MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> film was about 3~5. The MEMS pressure sensor based on novel MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanosheets was developed. The sensor showed a nonlinear error of 3.11%FS, a repeatability error of 1.75<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>FS, a hysteresis error of 0.74<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>FS, and basic accuracy of 3.64%FS.

articleTitle: Biosensor Based on Electrical Impedance Tomography for 3D Cancer Cell Culture Imaging
abstract: In this work, we proposed a biosensor based on 16 microelectrodes array for the monitoring of spheroid, a 3D cell culture model. It is based on electrical impedance tomography imaging, able to detect local change of electrical resistivity. First analysis, performed on 3D breast cancer cell culture proves this ability. The obtained change could be linked to local cell viability alteration.

articleTitle: On-Demand Provisioning of Wearable Sensors Data Processing Services in Edge Computing
abstract: The wearable sensor applications and services are highly sensible to computation latency. The infrastructure that processes data closer to its source or end user named as multi-access edge computing (MEC) has emerged to push the data processing services away from the centralized nodes to the network edge, enabling wearable sensor applications with the geolocation awareness. In this paper, we introduce on-demand provisioning of wearable sensors processing services in MEC system, a continuous deployment strategy that offer availability of wearable data processing services packaged as an application ready to be provisioned on-demand by the Docker container virtualization technique at the edge of the network. This allows, thus, fulfilling different requirements, such as low latency and accuracy.

articleTitle: Integrated Skin Microperfusion System for Lactate Concentration Monitoring
abstract: We developed a continuous lactate measurement system that integrates a microperfusion needle, a bubble removal channel, and an enzyme electrode sensor. The microperfusion needle has a microflow channel fabricated around a thin steel needle, which is covered by a perforated membrane. Using this flow channel, lactate can be collected from subepidermal tissue using the microperfusion method. The needle has sufficient rigidity to be inserted through the skin using an acupuncture needle. The concentration of collected lactate is measured by the enzyme electrode sensor, placed outside the body. This sensor is covered by a bubble-removal flow channel to remove bubbles and prevent them causing measurement noise on the electrode. Integration of the system allows real-time monitoring of lactate concentration in the skin. The bubble-removal flow channel removed bubbles effectively and the sensor had a sufficient measurement range to measure lactate concentration sampled by skin microperfusion. By measuring the perfusion pressure, we demonstrated that there was no leakage or clogging of the perfusate in this system.

articleTitle: Acoustofluidic Trapping in Structured Microchannels Using Lateral Transducer Modes
abstract: Acoustofluidic particle trapping in a circular resonant cavity in a microfluidic channel was performed using a lateral mode of two equal piezoceramic plate transducers. In order to achieve two-dimensional particle focusing in the cavity, the transducers were mounted to the chip with a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$90^{\circ}$</tex> tilt with respect to each other, so that each transducer is responsible for generating a standing wave either in the longitudinal or transversal direction with respect to the channel axis. The chip has multiple cavities with different diameters and thus different eigenfrequencies, which are arranged consecutively along a microfluidic channel. It was intended to trap particles dependent on the actuation frequencies at the corresponding resonant cavities. In the experiments described in this work trapping was only observed in one cavity, whose eigenfrequency matched the lateral transducer resonance. Due to low field intensity generated by the transducer, when driven off a resonance, particle trapping was not possible in the other cavities. Besides the cavity-trapping, we also found particle trapping within the channel sections connecting the individual cavities. By superposing a standing wave along the channel and a second one transversal to it, we achieved two-dimensional multi-nodal focusing here. We believe that the cavities partially act as acoustic reflectors thus supporting the formation of standing waves along the channel sections at certain frequencies. This phenomenon is not observed in this intensity in a straight channel without cavities.

articleTitle: Non-Invasive Monitoring of Swallowing Function Using Multi-Channel Auscultation
abstract: This study investigates a non-invasive and cost-effective solution for monitoring swallowing function by employing off-the-shelf microphones or digital stethoscopes, which could greatly benefit patients with dysphagia or related disorders and improve their care management. Our results demonstrated that superficial sounds recorded at the levels of thyroid cartilage, cricoid cartilage, sternum, and gastric cardia effectively reflected swallowing of three ingestibles with varying consistencies. Our results showed that one acoustic input was insufficient for identifying different ingestible consistencies. By employing an ensemble convolutional neural network with the spectra of all four sound channels as inputs, we successfully classified swallowing sounds associated with three distinct ingestible consistencies, achieving an average accuracy of 0.68 for cross-subject generalized model and 0.87 for cross-session personalized model. However, using superficial sounds recorded around thyroid cartilage level and sternum already offered comparable leave-one-out classification accuracy. This approach showcases the potential of using microphones for the clinical development of long-term bedside monitor for swallowing.

articleTitle: Ex-Situ Formed PANI/WS2 Composite for Improved Selectivity Towards Ammonia Gas
abstract: In this study, PANI was synthesized using oxidative polymerization while a colloidal method was followed to synthesize WS2. Subsequently, the two were used to form the PANI/WS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>composite ex-situ. The synthesized composite was used as a sensor to detect ammonia vapours at room temperature. The composite showed greater response to the ammonia vapours compared to pristine PANI and WS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. The improved response is attributed to the heterojunction as the electrons are transferred from p-to n-type material resulting in an increase in resistance and thus an increase in response. The properties of the PANI/WS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>composite based sensor were evaluated, and the sensor showed good selectivity, sensitivity, stability, and repeatability towards the ammonia vapours at room temperature.

articleTitle: A Disturbance Observer-Based Technique to Achieve System Modeling and Parameter Identification of Micro Heater
abstract: System modeling plays an important role in accomplishing the temperature control of the micro heater existing in the polymerase chain reactor (PCR). In this paper, a lumped mechanism model for the micro heater existing in the PCR system is first constructed, where some critical model parameters including the surface heat transfer coefficient and specific heat capacity are determined through a novel identification approaches simultaneously. Then, a disturbance observer (DO) that employs the input/output signal of the micro heater only is designed to estimate the lumped uncertainties caused by model errors, model uncertainties, external disturbances, and parameter perturbations. This estimates provided by the DO is added to the preliminary mechanism model of the micro heater to further improve the model' <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s$</tex> accuracy and reasonability. Experiments and comparisons between the mechanism model without the DO and the mechanism model with the DO are conduct to reveal the superiority of the proposed overall system modeling scheme.

articleTitle: Live Demonstration: Prevention and Prediction of Biomechanical Risks in Work Environment
abstract: Work-related musculoskeletal disorder (MSD) is one of the main issues faced by workers during their occupational life. People employed in industries, which require repetitive and manual lifting of loads, are the main subjects affected by this injury. Current solutions adopted to mitigate this risk have a qualitative approach and are not accurate enough. The proposed live demonstration shows an application of a real-time whole body articular stress analysis, estimated by means of wearable sensors and A.I. algorithms. In addition to the human state estimation, this work gives a new evaluation tool for the quantitative analysis of the MSD risk. Finally, A.I. algorithms for the online action recognition and the human risk prediction are shown within this live demonstration.

articleTitle: Design and Evaluation of a Miniaturized Non-Resonant Photoacoustic CO2 Gas Sensor with Integrated Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a miniaturized non-resonant photoacoustic CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>gas sensor with integrated electronics. The photoacoustic sensor (PAS) consists of a black body IR emitter, an appropriate optical filter, and a highly sensitive microphone, which converts the generated acoustic waves to electrical signals. The integrated electronics unit facilitates a standalone PAS sensor system, controls and powers the system components, and processes the electrical signals to provide a corresponding CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>gas concentration. The performance of the developed CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>PAS is evaluated and characterized. The measurements are done in the range of 0–9000 ppm. A sensitivity of 0.074 μV/ppm is achieved in the concentration range of 0–1537 ppm. For such a miniaturized non-resonant PAS sensor, the theoretical limit of detection (LOD) reaches 2.2 ppm for a sampling time of 330 seconds. Considering the cost, size, and performance, this sensor demonstrates the considerable potential for accurate and reliable indoor air quality monitoring.

articleTitle: Noninvasive Glucose Monitoring Evaluation with Diffused Transmitted NIRS in Soft Silicone-Based Tissue Phantoms
abstract: Solid tissue phantoms have been developed based on soft silicone elastomers with hydrophile additives, such as absorptive dyestuffs and glucose concentrations. For two prototypes of phantoms, we investigated the relative transmittance and extinction characteristics with transmitted near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) using an optical probe sensor. Notwithstanding the surface reflection and multiple scattering in solid tissue phantoms, we have successfully verified the performance of noninvasive glucose detection using a proposed normalized extinction difference method. The linear regression analysis for prediction glucose levels has shown a 0.99 adjusted coefficient of determination to reference glucose concentrations from 0 to 987 mg/dL.

articleTitle: Human-Inspired Stretch and Joint-Bend Sensing System Based on Flexible Sensors
abstract: Bio-mimicking of human tactile sensing system using flexible and reliable sensors and electrical circuits for developing future robots and prosthetics with better sensory capabilities has gained importance in recent times. In addition, development of artificial proprioception systems capable of locating, monitoring and controlling different parts and joints in robots is also vital. In this work, using a highly flexible, reliable, and easy to fabricate ecoflex-graphite-graphene carbon paste (GCP) based piezoresistive strain sensor, a Wheatstone bridge and a simulated leaky-integrate-and-fire (LIF) neuron, an artificial tactile system was developed which also includes the proprioception functionalities. The developed system generated neural spike trains when the sensor was strained, and the firing rates of the presented system varied between 7–26 spikes per min while increasing the strain levels from 5% to 50%. The spiking behaviour resembles an afferent neuron connected to a slowly-adapting mechanoreceptor. The relationships between firing rate with different stretch and bending angle in the sensor were also calculated to develop an artificial proprioception system. The presented work could pave the way for making next generation smart robots, prosthetics, gloves, and tactile sensors.

articleTitle: Polymer-Based Conductometric Sensor for Acidic and Alkaline Vapors for Firefighting and CBRN Disaster Control
abstract: Mobile sensors are highly sought-after for multiple applications. For example, in firefighting or CBRN disaster control the presence of acidic and alkaline gases, such as hydrogen chloride and ammonia, poses a significant threat to personnel, demanding fast responding mobile sensors. However, current gas sensors are often costly and react specifically to individual analytes, making them unsuitable for non-specialized first response units. This study presents a novel approach using a cost-effective and user-friendly gas sensor with direct electrical readout. It is based on a hygroscopic polyethylene glycol (PEG) layer on miniaturized interdigitated electrodes. The adsorbed water in the polymer rapidly undergoes pH changes upon exposure to pH-changing vapors, leading to a drastic change in conductivity of the PEG. The experimental results demonstrate the sensor's ability to detect relevant concentrations of pH-altering gases, with a response time comparable to commercial sensors.

articleTitle: Room Temperature Ammonia Sensor Based on Electrodeposited Polyaniline Film
abstract: Polyaniline (PANI) is a conducting polymer which has been widely used during the last decades in (bio)sensing applications. In the present work, a solution of aniline, camphorsulfonic acid and fluoral-p has been formulated and used as electrolyte for the electrochemical deposition of a porous film of PANI at the surface of a flexible interdigitated sensor device. Then, the ability of the electrodeposited PANI film to detect reducing ammonia gas was studied in the range 50–200 ppb. The resulting PANI-based sensor device exhibited high sensitivity to ammonia, good repeatability, and reversible response in a broad range of relative humidity.

articleTitle: OSC Based Gas Sensor for Detecting Agriculture Ammonia Water Pollution
abstract: Overabundant fertilization results in significant ammonia nitrogen pollution, which consequently triggers eutrophication. This study aims to tackle the constraints inherent in existing detection methodologies with an OSC based gas sensor, which can precisely detect 0.2 mg/L~20 mg/L ammonia nitrogen. To our knowledge, we are the first to successfully demonstrate the real-time detection of agriculture ammonia water pollution with solid state sensors.

articleTitle: Flexible Ag-Nanowire-Doped PEDOT:PSS Split Ring Resonator for Liquid Detection
abstract: Intrinsically conducting polymers render a promising alternative to conventional copper-based electronic devices, offering a solution to implement flexible devices. This study presents a non-intrusive liquid sensing setup comprised of a multilayer flexible split ring resonator as a sensing tag on a 50-Ohms-matched microstrip structure. The conductive layer of the proposed tag is fabricated using a flexible organic PEDOT:PSS material and highly conductive inorganic Ag nanowires to enhance the conductivity and flexibility of the polymeric structure. The fabricated sensor operates at the resonant frequency of 3.45 GHz with a resonant amplitude of −19.91 dB. The liquid sensing capability of the unbent tag is investigated using different volumes of standard liquids, including deionized water, ethanol, methanol, and isopropyl alcohol. Then, the proposed tag is wrapped around the exterior wall of a liquid container to demonstrate its sensing performance under bent condition. The integration of flexible and contactless microwave-based sensing capabilities makes the tag versatile and adaptable for various potential applications ranging from wearable sensors in healthcare monitoring to non-intrusive material characterization in chemical and pharmaceutical industries.

articleTitle: SSL-VoxPart: A Novel Solid-State LiDAR-Tailored Voxel Partition Approach for 3D Perception
abstract: LiDAR-based 3D point cloud segmentation is a crucial component in the perception system of many applications that rely on a thorough 3D environment understanding. LiDAR point clouds are unstructured, sparsely scattered in 3D space and have non-uniform densities, which restricts the use of ordinary convolutional neural networks. Tackling the point clouds irregular format, several approaches are introduced that divide the 3D space into a discretised volumetric grid. However, voxelization inevitably abandons the 3D topology of point clouds and suffers from information loss. In this paper, we propose SSL-VoxPart, a novel approach of scan-pattern related partitioning for voxel-wise semantic segmentation suitable to MEMS-actuated Solid-State LiDARs. We argue scan-pattern related voxel partitioning is worth being considered by showing improvements in extracting semantic information for voxel-wise point cloud segmentation, while reducing lossy cell-label encoding. We specifically conduct to the problems of crowded scene analysis. Crowds represent locally high density distributions of people with heavy occlusion effects, demanding for fine-grained predictions. We introduce a SSL data generation pipeline tailored to surveillance scenarios and validate our proposed method on the resulting dataset.

articleTitle: Real-Time Hyperspectral Imaging for Non-Invasive Monitoring of Tissue Ischemia
abstract: This paper presents a study on the use of hyperspectral imaging (HSI) for non-invasive, real-time monitoring of skin ischemia. We propose a novel ischemia index based on reflectance in a limited number of wavelengths, which can be calculated and visualized in real-time with low memory requirements. The index is tested on hyperspectral images of healthy and ischemic forearms, obtained by performing lower arm occlusion, and is compared to five other state-of-the-art indices from literature using binary support vector machines (SVMs). The results show that the proposed index is able to robustly distinguish between healthy and ischemic tissue in real-time, thus highlighting their potential to be used in a clinical setting.

articleTitle: Sensor Resistance Based Sensitivity Temperature Drift Tracking of Integrated 3D Hall Sensors
abstract: The magnetic sensitivity of voltage controlled Hall sensors changes up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 40\%$</tex> in the temperature range from −40°C to 125°C, resulting in large measurement errors. To track the temperature induced sensitivity variation, state of the art systems use additional temperature sensors and/or on-chip calibration coils. This paper presents a method to track the magnetic sensitivity temperature drift of a Hall sensor based on its own resistance. The proposed method results in a tracking accuracy of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm$</tex> 6% for Bx, By and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm$</tex> 3% for Bz in the temperature range from −40°C to 125°C. Providing a magnetic sensitivity to bias current transfer function further enhances the tracking accuracy to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\leq 1\%$</tex>. It requires no additional integrated coils or temperature sensors.

articleTitle: Analog Pyroelectric Infrared Sensor for Non-Invasive Beehive Monitoring
abstract: Honeybees flying in front of a beehive were observed by the unconventional use of an analog output pyroelectric infrared (PIR) sensor. A microprocessor calculated the temperature-corrected variance of the sensor's analog output voltage to quantify the bee activity level. Sensor data were transmitted via a WiFi link to an Internet-of-Things (IoT) platform for remote real-time monitoring and data analysis. The technique was sufficiently sensitive to detect individual flying bees, swarming, robbing, and other intrusive apiary events. The sensor performance was equivalent to considerably more expensive radar, vibration, or video beehive monitoring systems.

articleTitle: Optical CMOS Transceiver with $8\times 32$ SPAD Array, 32 TDCs and Laser Diode Driver for Wearable Time-Domain Diffuse Optics Applications
abstract: A single-chip optical transceiver for wearable time-domain diffuse optics healthcare applications has been fabricated in 150 nm CMOS technology. The chip includes an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{8}\times \mathbf{32}$</tex> single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) array with 32 time-to-digital converters (TDC) with ~60 ps resolution and a laser diode driver which can produce short ~0.5 A current pulses at a repetition rate of 15 MHz. The measured instrument response function (IRF) of the transceiver was measured to be ~120 ps with a laser pulse width of 90 ps and a wavelength of 854 nm.

articleTitle: Live Demonstration: Soft Flexible Capacitive Sensing Arrays for Pressure, Shear, and Proximity
abstract: Soft flexible capacitive sensors are demonstrated that can capture a combination of pressure, shear, and proximity information intended for medical, sports and robotics applications. They consist of three major components—silicone elastomer, conductive fabric, and flexible printed circuit boards (FPCB). Empowered by a custom readout circuit utilizing the Cypress PSoC 6 MCU, the systems consume 20 mW while scanning and transmitting measurement data via Bluetooth Low-Energy (BLE) 5.0. Pressure, shear, and proximity are visualized in a custom mobile application. Operation of our wearable and industrial sensors is shown.

articleTitle: 3D-Printer-Based Test-Bench for Contactless Respiratory Monitoring Systems
abstract: Respiratory monitoring is becoming an interesting research topic in many areas (health care, automotive, and aviation). One of the most prominent non-contact technologies is mm-wave radar, which allows real-time thoracic skin mm-movements tracking. The following work focuses on developing a test-bench to verify the performance of a breathing rate monitoring device based on a mm-wave radar. The innovative element of the setup concerns a 3D printer programmed by an automatic geometric code (G-code) generation tool that converts an ordered sequence of arbitrary temporal-position coordinates into a series of low-level instructions for reproducing the movement. A dielectric skin-equivalent dummy completes the test-bench and is used in the final stage to validate a 60 GHz radar-based system simulating respiratory displacement with physiological amplitudes and frequencies.

articleTitle: Gas Sensor Based on Nonlinear Coupled AlN-Piezoelectric Micromachined Resonators
abstract: This paper reports a novel Aluminium-Nitride (AlN)-based piezoelectric micromachined gas sensor relying on thermal energy dissipation (heating or cooling) of an electrically heated weakly coupled resonator. The coupled MEMS resonator, consisting of a bridge and cantilever resonators mechanically coupled, was driven by applying AC voltage to an AlN-piezoelectric layer coated on the clamped-clamped beam. The frequency and the velocity spectra are studied with a laser Doppler vibrometer. The buckling behaviour of the devices under high electrothermal voltage was analyzed. Moreover, two modes veering phenomena were observed and discussed. Sensing performance for two operation points before and after the buckling point was explored experimentally for increasing concentrations of Helium. The results yield different directions of frequency shift with 3.123<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>/kHz and 1.089<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>/kHz slope respectively, showing the great potential for high-performance gas sensing.

articleTitle: Rapid Detection of Escherichia Coli Using Graphene Oxide Based Electrochemical Sensor Chip
abstract: Detection of E. coli bacteria is imperative when it comes to potable water cleanliness and human health. E. coli when present in drinking water can cause ill health and its presence in urine is an indication of Urinary Tract Infection (UTI). This paper reports the development of rapid, easy to use, and low cost electrochemical sensor for detection of E.coli. The sensor is fabricated by drop casting graphene oxide (GO) on the screen printed carbon electrodes. Different bacteria dilutions were mixed with a fixed concentration of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. Graphene oxide sheets allow for the indirect detection of bacteria by reducing the remaining concentration of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> following the bacterial catalytic activity. This work presents GO synthesis, characterization, sample preparation and bacterial testing using H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> degradation. The sensor provides a response within a range of 0 to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.7 \times 10^{3}$</tex> CFU/mL and has a detection limit of 6.3 CFU/mL. The amount of time required for both response and recovery of the sensor is measured in milliseconds.

articleTitle: Yttrium Iron Garnet Magnetometers with $1\ \text{nT}/\sqrt{Hz}$ Sensitivity
abstract: Yttrium iron garnet is a ferrimagnetic material suitable for spin wave devices capable of operating over a very wide range from very low up to terahertz and optical frequencies. Here we discuss for the first time optical and microwave YIG magnetometers with very high unshielded sensitivities approaching 1 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{nT}/\sqrt{\boldsymbol{Hz}}$</tex>. The microwave YIG magnetometer consists of a quarter-wavelength <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\boldsymbol{\lambda}/\mathbf{4})$</tex> microstripline resonator at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{f}_{\boldsymbol{r}}\sim \mathbf{2}.\mathbf{9}\ \boldsymbol{GHz}$</tex> with a YIG section near its grounded tip. A biasing magnet <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\boldsymbol{B}_{\boldsymbol{e}})$</tex> was used to tune the YIG's ferromagnetic resonance to coincide with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\boldsymbol{f}_{\boldsymbol{r}})$</tex> resulting in ~ -110 dB insertion loss at resonance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\boldsymbol{I}_{\boldsymbol{r}})$</tex>. We then measured <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{I}_{\boldsymbol{r}}$</tex> to sense the external magnetic flux density <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\boldsymbol{B}_{\boldsymbol{e}}).\boldsymbol{I}_{\boldsymbol{r}}$</tex> changed to -78 dB when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{B}_{\boldsymbol{e}}\sim \mathbf{10}\ \boldsymbol{nT}$</tex> was applied. The optical YIG magnetometer consists of a laser with a circularly polarized beam passing through the YIG sample. The external field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{B}_{\boldsymbol{e}}$</tex>, in this case, applies a torque on laser-generated spins inside YIG and results in the reduction of the transmitted laser power. The circularly polarized laser can also be used to change YIG's magnetization.

articleTitle: Development of a Paper based Glutathione Detection for Point of Care Low Resource Settings
abstract: Rapid, sensitive, and cost-effective point of care solutions are the key to early diagnosis of disease biomarkers, even in remote or low resource settings. Thus, the present work integrates the advantages of paper flow devices for the point of care glutathione detection. Glutathione is a vital non protein compound present in the circulatory system whose deficiency may lead to a spectrum of health conditions such as, neurodegenerative diseases, cardiovascular diseases, hepatic disorders, autoimmune diseases, ageing, diabetes etc. Hence, the capability to detect blood or cellular glutathione acts as an early marker for several diseases and their progression. The present device is engineered to detect the molar concentration of glutathione using enzyme mimetic property of BSA- MnO2 nanoparticles combined with d 3,3, 5,5 - tetramethylbenzidine (TMB), to form an oxidized TMB (a blue colored product). The blue color product, which is functionalized onto paper substrates form a colorimetric detection scheme. The analyte containing glutathione is then dispensed on to the sensing zone of the device. The strength of de-coloration indicates the concentration of the glutathione. The colorimetric changes are further noted by acquiring an image of the sensing zone and processing the respective standalone GSH concentration through an application software.

articleTitle: Low-Bow Glass-Si Anodic Wafer Bonding at High Temperature by Means of CTE Engineering of Corning Novel Fusion Glass
abstract: In this study, a nearly bow-free anodic bond with high bond strength using SUSS MicroTec manual wafer bonder between Si and SG3.3+ fusion glass from Corning Inc. by means of CTE tailoring of the glass wafer is presented. In BF33 glass wafers used widely in the MEMS industry, due to the CTE mismatch with Si wafer, anodic bond temperature should be kept at < 300°C to minimize the unwanted bonded stack bow after the cool-down step. This could lead to a large decrease in bond strength and even resulting in some unbonded areas. In the new SG3.3+ glass type, owing to its novel manufacturing procedure, further heat-treatment (annealing) of the glass wafer after manufacturing and prior to bonding is possible. This will result in an excellent CTE match between this glass type and that of Si at ideal bonding temperature. Therefore, anodic bonding at high temperature of 350°C will result in a rather bowless bonded stack with very high bond strength. The details of the glass heat-treatment as well as the bonding parameters, CTE and bow values are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Wireless, Battery-Free, Multi-Modal Sensor System for Continuous Monitoring of Physiological Signals of Paraplegic Patients
abstract: Wireless, battery-free, skin-mountable pressure sensing systems that enable continuous and accurate measurement of pressure at skin interfaces hold immense potential in preventing the development of pressure injuries. However, there are still significant challenges in continuously tracking pressure with high sensitivity and stability over the required pressure range at critical sites for individuals sitting in wheelchairs. This research paper introduces a wireless, battery-free, multimodal sensor system designed for continuous measurement of pressure and temperature at specific locations of interest on human subjects, whether they are moving or stationary in a wheelchair. The pressure sensor incorporates a cracked metal film, which serves as the active layer, encapsulated with a passivation layer. Its design allows for membrane deflection, enabling excellent sensitivity, low hysteresis, and long-term stability over the pressure range necessary for this application. Moreover, the battery-free, wireless platform and movable sensing system provide stable and long-range communication capabilities at multiple mounting locations, accommodating both moving and stationary scenarios. Experimental evaluations of the pressure sensor and movable system include benchtop measurements, which are further validated through numerical simulations to showcase the functionality of the system. Finally, clinical trials involving patients with spinal cord injuries in wheelchairs demonstrate the feasibility and stability of the sensor and movable system in preventing pressure injuries acquired from sitting.

articleTitle: Low Power Flexible MXene-Graphene Oxide Based Heaters for Wearable Clothing
abstract: This research paper examines the remarkable potential of MXene-based cloth heaters, an innovative technology set to redefine the concept of personal warmth at low cost. MXene (composites), a group of two-dimensional materials consisting of transition metal carbides, nitrides, and carbonitrides, have garnered significant attention for their outstanding electrical conductivity, flexibility, and heat generation capabilities. Capitalizing on these unique properties, we have developed cloth heaters infused with MXene, offering unparalleled comfort, efficiency, and adaptability as compared to conventional flexible heaters.
