This paper explores the scientific principles that underlie MXene-Graphene oxide (MXGO)-based cloth heaters with methyl cellulose improving the mechanical stability, providing insights into simple deposition technique on fabrics, optimization in the composite and versatile applications characterized by cyclic stability, low power (0.4W) with a maximum efficiency of 84.4% at −10°C and 97.1 % on human skin as compared to ambient (27°C). The stability test showed temperature variation of ±2% when tested for a duration of 24hrs in a Peltier system at −10°C. Furthermore, it explores the tremendous potential of this emerging technology to revolutionize various sectors like military applications (where soldiers have to live in extreme cold temperatures), outdoor apparel, medical textiles, and smart woven fabrics.

articleTitle: Integration of Thin Film Electrodes for Microfluidic Electrochemical Cells
abstract: In this work, we develop processes for integration of thin film TiW-Au and Ti-Pt electrodes in microfluidic electrochemical cells for multiparametric and parallelized analyses in flow. We discuss the reliability of the developed patterning processes and present a preliminary electrochemical characterization of these electrodes when patterned on planar and non-planar surfaces. This work is a response to a growing trend towards miniaturization, digitalization, and multitasking in electrochemistry.

articleTitle: Wireless Skin Temperature Monitoring for Microwave Hyperthermia: Feasibility Study of an Epidermal RFID Sensor Grid
abstract: Microwave hyperthermia is an emerging anticancer therapy with the potential to improve the outcomes of chemotherapy and radiation therapy. However, the application of microwave energy to the skin can cause thermal damage and discomfort to patients. To address this issue, a novel epidermal RFID-based Thermal Monitoring Sheet (R-TMS) is proposed as a wireless, low-cost, and non-invasive solution for monitoring skin temperature during the treatment. R-TMS is a planar grid of RFID antennas embedded with temperature-sensing Integrated Circuits (ICs), operating in the UHF band, and designed to be placed in direct contact with the skin to provide a real-time temperature spatial map. Simulations demonstrated that the R-TMS introduces minimal variations in the Effective Field Size (EFS) and Effective Heating Depth (EHD), indicating its compatibility with the therapy. Moreover, Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) distribution analysis revealed a slight local increment in SAR on the skin, but the resulting temperature rise variation remained within acceptable limits. Finally, experimental measurements preliminary demonstrate its accuracy and reliability for skin temperature monitoring.

articleTitle: Optimizing Spatial Sensing Performance with Kriging and SRGAN – A Feasibility Study
abstract: Several studies have aimed at improving sensor performance through deep learning. In this paper, we explore the feasibility of using advanced machine learning techniques, specifically Kriging and Super Resolution Generative Adversarial Networks, to enhance the performance and accuracy of simulated force sensitive resistor matrices with a low number of sensors. Kriging is a geostatistical method that uses spatial correlations to interpolate or predict values at unsampled locations, while Super Resolution Generative Adversarial Networks are a type of generative adversarial network that can generate high-resolution images from low-resolution inputs. Our results suggest that machine learning techniques can provide a powerful tool for enhancing the accuracy performance of force sensing technologies, with potential applications in a wide range of fields, especially in autonomous vehicles.

articleTitle: Ultraviolet vs. Visible Skylight Polarization Measurements
abstract: Concerning autonomous navigation in GNSS-denied environments, insects like bees, ants, locusts and butterflies are certainly the cup winners. Bees and some ants are known to be sensitive to polarized light, both in ultraviolet (UV) and visible spectra, and to use it for their outside moving heading calculation. Therefore, we chose to compare UV and visible skylight polarization measurements in order to understand how UV could be used to improve heading estimation by processing the skylight's angle of polarization patterns. We then used a commercial polarimetric camera sensitive to visible polarized light and a UV-sensitive camera enhanced with polarized light measurement ability.

articleTitle: Towards Photon-Noise Limited Thermal IR Detection with Optomechanical Resonators
abstract: In this study, we propose an advancement of the state-of-the-art uncooled thermal IR sensing utilizing silicon nitride nano-optomechanical resonators integrated with a broadband absorber layer of platinum. By characterizing the frequency stability and relative responsivity to impinging electromagnetic power of our sensors, we determine a noise equivalent power (NEP) as low as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$275\ pW/\sqrt{Hz}$</tex>. Our findings contribute to the development of high-sensitivity uncooled thermal IR detectors, potentially eliminating the reliance on cryogenic cooling, towards the photon-noise limit.

articleTitle: HFR Video-Based Hornet Detection Approach Using Wing-Beat Frequency Analysis
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to effectively detect and distinguish honeybees and hornets by analyzing their wing-beat frequency based on high-frame-rate videos. First, we extract foreground objects that possibly contain insects by using the K-nearest neighbor algorithm. Hungarian algorithm is applied to calculate the correspondence relation between centroids from different video frames. Thereafter, we calculate the centroid displacement of these foreground contours and obtain their displacement signals. We then filter these signals through the empirical mode decomposition method to exclude the global movement components. Finally, we examined the filtered signals using Fast Fourier Transform to identify the characteristic flapping frequency of different bee species. We conducted several field experiments to evaluate our method. The result proves the feasibility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Sensors for General Health Diagnostics Using Biomarkers in Bodily Fluids
abstract: The development of sensors for simple and low-cost everyday general health self-testing is receiving increasing attention. A key approach involves the detection of biomarkers levels in various bodily fluids: blood, urine, sweat, saliva [1]. Hormones produced by glands in the endocrine system and neurotransmitters produced by the nervous system control many bodily functions. The concentrations of these molecules in the body are an indication of its state, hence the use of the term biomarker. Excess concentrations of biomarkers, such as cortisol, serotonin, epinephrine, dopamine, are released by the body in response to a variety of conditions - emotional state (euphoria, stress), disease, etc. The development of simple, low-cost modalities for point-of-use (PoU) measurements of biomarkers levels in various bodily fluids (blood, urine, sweat, saliva) as opposed to conventional hospital or lab settings is receiving increasing attention. First, a review is presented of the basic properties of primary stress-related biomarkers: origin in the body (i.e. if they are produced as hormones, neurotransmitters or both), chemical composition, molecular weight (small or medium size molecules and polymers, ranging from ~ 100Da to ~ 100kDa), hydro- or lipo-philic nature [1].

articleTitle: Analysis of Liquid Morphologies in Curved Open Microchannels
abstract: Liquids show spontaneous capillary filling if the total energy of the system is minimized by the filling process. While the evaluation of this is straightforward for closed round microgrooves and leads to Washburn's equation, the treatment of open curved microgrooves is more challenging. Both, the exposed liquid surface and the additional curvature influence the liquid morphology. In this work we introduce a method for the prediction of the occurrence of spontaneous capillary flow by analyzing liquid morphologies inside the microgrooves using Gradient Descent simulations. We show how this method can be applied to winding microgrooves and determine the influence of the liquid front on the capillary filling process.

articleTitle: Live Demonstration: Coupled-Core Fiber Bragg Grating Sensors
abstract: Coupled-core fibers are waveguides that comprise two or more cores close to each other. Bragg gratings inscribed in such fibers exhibit unique features that can be exploited for sensing purposes. For example, bending or vibrations can alter the reflectivity of the Bragg gratings while temperature changes the wavelength position of the grating. To monitor reflectivity changes, a compact, high-speed, and cost-effective interrogation unit was developed. In this live demonstration, force, touch, and impact sensors that can distinguish the direction of the force or impact will be presented.

articleTitle: Automated Line Detection on Lateral Flow Assays: A Paradigm Shift in Rapid Diagnostic Testing
abstract: Lateral flow assays (LFAs) provide rapid, accurate, and affordable results for disease diagnostics in resource-limited and point-of-care settings. However, the manual interpretation of LFA results can introduce human errors and biases. In this paper, we detail an automated line detection system that can read and interpret LFA results based on the image taken using a smartphone or any other digital imaging device. The proposed system can self identify the test and control lines of the LFA and can be used to quantify the analyte post calibration The automated line detection system reduces the reliance on trained personnel and enhances the accuracy and reliability of LFA readouts. This work details the various steps from image acquisition to detection of the test and control lines of a sensitive LFA and also evaluated an increase in sensitivity of detection due to the readout automation. In conclusion, the automated line detection can generate more accurate and consistent data than manual interpretation, which can be used to make better decisions for patient care.

articleTitle: Live Demonstration: ORIGIN - Optical Fibre Sensors for Radiation Dose Mapping and Source Localisation During Brachytherapy
abstract: ORIGIN is a European H2020 funded research project aimed at improving brachytherapy, a precise type of internal radiotherapy, in the treatment of prostate and gynecological cancer. A novel multichannel optical fibre sensor system has been developed to provide real-time monitoring of the radiation dose delivered to the patient during treatment. Through machine learning algorithms, the radiation source(s) location is determined and a 3D map of the dose delivered to the tumor and nearby organs at risk, e.g. urethra, bladder, rectum, is developed. Real-time in vivo dosimetry allows for a dose-led, patient-oriented treatment plan, leading to enhanced treatment safety and improved patient outcomes.

articleTitle: Lane Detection and Estimation from Surround View Camera Sensing Systems
abstract: Autonomous driving poses unique challenges for vehicle environment perception systems. It is highly desirable that we utilize existing vehicle-equipped driver-assistant sensors, without hardware change, to achieve driverless performance. Current product level vehicle surround view camera module (denoted concisely as SVS) is served as a panoramic view visual aid tool for low-automation applications. With proper statistical analysis, the multiple mono-camera information can be very useful for higher vehicle intelligence without significant hardware change. In this study, we focus on lane detection and estimation from a SVS only system. The major difficulty lies in the fact that mono-cameras of the SVS are non-cooperative and essentially of protractor nature; this would lead to large uncertainty on object depth information and incomplete lane observations. We process the highly distorted data in a multi-stage manner. We first utilize a neural network classifier to yield labeled lane-relevant objects. The lane <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex>ark<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s$</tex>/edges point clouds are processed by a truncated Gaussian random field model for the spatial filtering and a fading memory model for the temporal filtering. Then we present polynomial fitting scheme and a statistical analysis of the fitting errors reveals good lane and ego-vehicle orientation cues. In a parking lot real world study, we show promising lane detection and estimation performance of significant practical implications for lane keeping capability in high-automation applications.

articleTitle: A Quantitative Identification of “Moist Feeling” by High-Resolution Tactile Sensor Devices
abstract: In this paper, we report on a method for measuring and quantitatively evaluating “Moist Feeling,” which is said to be one of the most important and complex tactile senses, using a high-resolution tactile sensor. We have focused on the adsorption friction characteristics of materials and have succeeded in identifying presence of “Moist” based on the characteristic behavior of the friction coefficient at low loads. In this paper, we have established an evaluation method for “Moist Feeling” and worked on quantification of “Moist Feeling” by using this evaluation method for two types of materials: one with moisture added and the other without moisture added, which changes the feel to the touch. This is an example of previously unknown knowledge about the “Moist Feeling”, and the MEMS tactile sensor and evaluation method in this study will bring us much closer to the realization of the quantification of the “Moist Feeling”.

Author Keywords: quantification of the sense of touch

articleTitle: Sensitivity-Enhanced Piezoelectric Humidity Sensor Based on a Parity Time Symmetric System Biased at the Exceptional Point
abstract: A sensitivity-enhanced piezoelectric sensor is developed based on a parity time (PT) symmetric system. The PT symmetric system operates in the vicinity of the exceptional point (EP), where the eigenvalues undergo a translation from real to complex. The translation is companied by an ultra-high sensitivity to small perturbations, so that the PT system is ultra-sensitive compared with the traditional piezoelectric sensors. In this paper, the PT symmetric system consists of a piezoelectric resonator coupled with an LCR tank, in which the resistance is replaced by a negative resistance circuit. Theoretical analysis, simulation and experiment are conducted on the PT symmetric system with a PZT piezoelectric resonator. The sensitivity can be enlarged up to three times compared to the traditional single piezoelectric resonator under the small humidity perturbation.

articleTitle: Flight-Testing of a MEMS Wall Shear Stress Thermal Sensor on a Microlight Aircraft
abstract: This paper reports the realization of thermal MEMS (Micro Electro-Mechanical Systems) sensors designed for wall shear stress measurement during real flight on a microlight aircraft. Based on constant temperature anemometry and calorimetric principle, the micro-sensors measure the viscous shear stress occurring at the wall of a structure interacting with a fluid flow and detect the flow direction. A proper packaging was realized for ensuring a flush but robust integration of the devices on a pod fixed on a microlight aircraft. Real flight-testing demonstrated the ability of the micro-sensors to realize aerodynamic measurements up to 250 km/h on the microlight aircraft.

articleTitle: Robust Multi-layer Kevlar Aerogel for High Performance Force Sensor
abstract: To meet the increasing application of wearable force sensors, there is an urgent demanding for developing flexible and light-weight base materials for the application. To improve the detection limit of the force sensors, the mechanical strength of base material needs to be optimized. Kevlar nanofibers are great candidates for fabricating aerogels due to the lightweight, great thermal stability and good compatibility to multiple nanofiller. But single layer Kevlar-based aerogel film is fragile and easily disturbed by environmental conditions. Here in, we develop an assemble strategy to fabricate multilayer aerogel film. Single layer aerogel film is fabricated by blade-coating and freeze-drying strategies with different nanofiller to functionalize the aerogel film. Different functional layer stack, with Kevlar nanofiber dispersions with lower density filling in the interlayer. Then the aerogel was hot-pressed and dried. The multi-layer aerogel film exhibits great mechanical strength, with an improvement of 27% and 166% of strain and stress, respectively. The construction of the multi-layer aerogel indicates a great potential in wearable force sensors.

articleTitle: Noise and Gaussian Clutter Background Descending Dimensional Subspace Signal Detector
abstract: This paper deals with the detection of subspace signals in the context of noise and Gaussian clutter. Classical detectors usually treat clutter and noise as a whole, assuming a set of independent identically distributed (IID) training data without signal components to estimate the covariance matrix of clutter and noise. However, in practical applications, it is usually difficult to obtain sufficient training data, hence, we propose a generalized likelihood ratio test (GLRT) detector based on a one-step design strategy in the context of noise and Gaussian clutter, assuming that the Gaussian clutter covariance matrix has a presymmetric structure, and using a dimensionality reduction method of subspace transformation. Theoretical analysis shows that the detector has a constant false alarm rate property for the covariance matrix of clutter plus noise. Simulation analysis shows that the detector can work properly in the absence of training data, and the detection performance is better than existing comparison detectors.

articleTitle: Significant Improvement in Precision of Real-Time Blood Pressure Prediction Based on Complete Cycles of Measured PPGs
abstract: A novel approach is presented for accurate and continuous monitoring of blood pressure (BP) using photoplethysmography (PPG) signals. The limitations of previous methodologies in accurately distinguishing between qualified and unqualified PPG waveforms, particularly in terms of complete cycles, have undermined the accuracy of BP estimations. To address this, a two-stage deep learning model combining 1D-CNN and LSTM for PPG quality assessment and 1D-CNN and GRU for BP estimation is proposed. Experimental results show that the 1D-CNN model achieves a high classification accuracy of 98.39% for PPG signal quality assessment. Without PPG quality assessment, the mean error (ME) ± standard deviation (SD) for systolic blood pressure (SBP) and diastolic blood pressure (DBP) is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.31\pm 9.84$</tex> mmHg and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.19\pm 5.75$</tex> mmHg, respectively. However, with the implementation of PPG quality assessment, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{ME}\pm \text{SD}$</tex> for SBP is reduced to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.47\pm 6.23$</tex> mmHg, and for DBP to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.23\pm 3.93$</tex> mmHg, respectively. These results highlight the effectiveness of the proposed method, providing a promising strategy for accurate, real-time, and continuous blood pressure monitoring based on complete cycles of measured PPGs.

articleTitle: Enhancing Positioning Sensor Applications: Online Harmonic Order Determination of Atan2-Function
abstract: This study introduces novel techniques for improving error correction in actuator applications using rotary positioning sensors. It addresses challenges related to harmonic distortions and the inhomogeneous sampling of sensor signals. Our approaches include interpolation methods and Kalman filtering, capable of reducing the inhomogeneous sampling and identifying the most significant harmonic order. The developed methods demonstrate high stability with efficient sample sizes and a small distance factor. These enhancements significantly reduce shape change and offer accurate identification of the most significant harmonic order, contributing to improved sensor accuracy and actuation performance in vehicle applications.

articleTitle: Real-time Resonance Frequency Tracking in Photoacoustic Spectroscopy for Gas Detection
abstract: Photoacoustic spectroscopy (PAS) for gas detection usually employs acoustic or mechanical resonators to amplify the photoacoustic signal, enabling detection at ultra-low concentrations. However, the frequency drift in resonant systems can significantly impact the accuracy and stability. This paper proposes a novel approach for realtime tracking of the resonance frequency by locking the phase difference between the sensor's output and the modulation signal. The methodology was validated by implementing it in a PAS system equipped with an acoustic resonator. The experimental results demonstrate that the closed-loop frequency tracking function reduces the temperature drift coefficient by 51%, significantly improving the stability of the resonant PAS system.

articleTitle: Enhancing Anti-Icing Performance of Sensors with Thermoresponsive-Superhydrophobic Hybrid Surfaces
abstract: Ice accumulation on the sensors operating under low temperatures degrades sensing performance, resulting in the deterioration of data reliability. Although the superhydrophobic surfaces enable excellent freezing delay, it impedes droplet evaporation in the deicing process for full-drying. For enhancing the deicing performance while maintaining the anti-icing capabilities, diverse strategies should be considered and investigated. Recently, the hybrid wettability surfaces have been highlighted due to their excellent deicing performance with minimal sacrifice in the freezing delay. Herein, we discuss the anti-icing characteristics of hybrid surfaces which have stripe patterns with superhydrophobic and thermoresponsive zones. In low temperature, the thermoresponsive zone shows hydrophobicity(142°) and changes to hydrophilic(65°) at high temperature. The hybrid surfaces are successfully fabricated by coating two different layers on the roughened surfaces. The fabricated surfaces show excellent freezing delay capability exhibiting a frost density of 150.6 kg/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> similar to that of the superhydrophobic surfaces. Furthermore, they improve deicing characteristics by reducing deicing time by 57.1% compared to the superhydrophobic surfaces upon the changes in the wettability of the thermoresponsive region.

articleTitle: Strain Microsensors Based on Carbon Nanotube/Polyimide Thin Films
abstract: The work shows the process for the fabrication of strain sensors using a 5 µm thick polyimide film loaded with 3 % weight carbon nanotubes as piezoresistive material. The sensors were produced using standard photolithography techniques, which allowed a reliable structuring of meanders with a linewidth of 50 µm and a line aspect ratio of 1:10. The thin film sensors were tested under tensile 1% strain for their characterization. The gauge factor of the produced sensors was k ~ 30. The sensors exhibited a slight drift of their electrical resistance after repeated tensile cycles. It was also noticed that their electrical resistance is influenced by the temperature with a negative dependence. These results help to establish the possibilities of integrating polymer nanocomposites for the development of strain sensors.

articleTitle: Live Demonstration: Mobile Environmental Monitoring System
abstract: Air pollution is a pressing challenge in high density cities. Advanced environmental monitoring technologies and data-driven approaches are crucial for addressing this issue and promoting sustainable urban environments. Traditional stationary monitoring stations have limitations in capturing the dynamic nature of air pollution across different locations, leading to an incomplete understanding of overall air quality. To overcome this, mobile environmental monitoring systems are emerging as innovative solutions.

articleTitle: A Thermal Microfluidic Flow Sensor Screen-Printed onto an Ultrathin PMMA Foil
abstract: This paper reports on the devised fabrication procedure and experimental investigation and characterization of a thermal based flow sensor for microfluidic systems based on polymer technology. The sensor itself is screen-printed onto a self-fabricated ultrathin polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) foil, which minimizes the heat capacity and therefore yields fast response times of integrated thermal transducers. Integrating the foil-based sensor into the center of a PMMA stack consisting of a substrate and a top plate (both preprocessed to form a microfluidic channel) enables a suitable material compatibility and a low-cost fabrication procedure. Using the well-known evaluation principles of thermal anemometers, the four-wire sensor can be used for accurate flow measurements in such polymer-based microfluidic systems, where the measurement range of the sensor is easily adaptable by changing the channel's height. Currently, it is possible to measure flows starting in the range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10\ \mu\mathrm{l}$</tex> per minute up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1000\ \mu\mathrm{l}$</tex> per minute.

articleTitle: Energy-Efficient Sensor Platform using Reliable Analog-to-Feature Extraction
abstract: Analog compute-in-memory (ACIM)-based sensor platform enables simultaneous feature extraction and data dimension reduction on analog data, resulting in significant energy savings. This paper explores the energy and task performance in ACIM-based sensor platform and investigates their trade-off across different data dimension reduction rates. A feature restoration (FR) network is also proposed to improve the distorted features from ACIM. Simulation results show a 77.9% energy savings (48.5% if FR is implemented in sensor) with 2.4% accuracy drop compared to the baseline scenario of digitizing the entire input data and transmitting to the processing node.

articleTitle: CMOS Transceiver with Time-Gated 4×8 SPAD Array and Width-Controlled Laser Diode Pulser for Time-Domain Diffuse Optics Measurements
abstract: A CMOS transceiver for time-domain diffuse optics measurements has been fabricated with 150 nm CMOS technology on a single die. The pulse width of a laser diode (LD) can be adjusted from 835 ps to 3 ns, with a resolution of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 100$</tex> ps, for different types of LDs. The time-gated and time-resolved <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4\times 8$</tex> SPAD array can be loaded to Geiger mode within less than 150 ps. The TDC can capture returning photons with a resolution of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 52.46$</tex> ps, and the data is stored in 128 14-bit counters. The repetition rate can be up to 12.5 MHz. At a 1 Hz sample rate, with 1 000 000 pulses, the average power consumption of the transceiver was 25.76 mW, excluding the FPGA controller.

articleTitle: Improved Signal Processing Algorithm to Enhance the Performance of Electrostatic Sensors for Particle Velocity Measurement
abstract: This paper proposes an improved cross-correlation signal processing algorithm for the velocity measurement of pneumatically conveyed solids using electrostatic sensors. The proposed algorithm increases the measurement accuracy in noisy environments and improves the dynamic response for real-time applications. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm was evaluated through computer simulation and experimental tests.

articleTitle: Making A Microwave Sandwich from Tunable Impedance Sheets for Complex Permittivity Extraction
abstract: This study presents a method for extracting the complex permittivity of an unknown material positioned between two tunable impedance sheets. By illuminating this configuration with a transceiver antenna and monitoring the changes in the resonant profile of the reflected signal over the tunable space, the complex permittivity of the unknown material can be determined. This method was investigated using pairs of inductive and capacitive impedance sheets that were used to sandwich dielectric materials with permittivities up to 10 and loss tangents up to 0.4. Here we show that inductive sandwiching sheets provide higher sensitivity with respect to loss tangent than capacitive sandwiching sheets; however, the range of detectable values is more limited. This method requires only scalar reflection measurements and therefore provides a low-cost method of wireless complex permittivity extraction.

articleTitle: Live Demonstration: Low-Power Flexible Platform for Laser-Scribed Graphene Sensors
abstract: Laser-scribed graphene-based sensors provide inherent flexible capabilities when fabricated in polyimide substrate. However, this capability is lost when paired with readout systems manufactured in rigid printed circuit boards. Using the same substrate during fabrication achieves a fully flexible approach with its circuitry and sensing material. Thus, a complete sensing system can be fabricated in the same material yielding a much faster and easier combination of the sensor and its interface. Furthermore, this flexible platform can be easily integrated into wearable applications, in which the conformation of the system provides comfort for the user creating a better experience when using the platform.

articleTitle: Two-Dimensional Waterflow Sensor Using Multiple Absolute Pressure Sensors
abstract: This study reports a two-dimensional (2D) waterflow sensor for marine aquaculture. In recent years, environmental monitoring has been widely developed in marine aquaculture. Among these monitoring, ocean currents are one of the important factors in capturing the inflow of hypoxic water into fish cages. However, there were no low-power, simple waterflow sensors that could be adapted to fish cages. Here we propose a waterflow sensor using with a cylindrical housing and an array of six absolute pressure sensor elements to measure 2D waterflow velocity around a fish cage. 2D waterflow velocity is calculated via a polynomial regression model of the responses of six pressure sensors and sensor tilt angle. By constructing the model for each tilt angle, the developed sensor responded with sufficient sensitivity to waterflow velocities from 0.4 to 2.0 m/s.

articleTitle: Bout-based Gas Source Localization using Aerial Robot Swarms
abstract: Gas source localization (GSL) helps mitigate the impact of industrial accidents and natural disasters. While GSL may be dangerous and time-consuming when performed by humans, swarms of agile and inexpensive nano aerial robots may increase the safety and efficiency of gas source localizations. Since the small payloads of nano aerial robots limit the sensing and computing resources, strategies adapted from biological swarms, such as colonies of social insects, are used to coordinate robot swarms. Most swarm GSL strategies are based on the assumption that the maxima of gas concentrations are sufficiently close to the gas sources. However, prior studies have indicated that the occurrence of “bouts”, a metric for the intermittency of gas distributions, may advantageously be used as a more accurate gas source proximity indicator. This paper presents a swarm GSL strategy employing bouts as source proximity indicators and a bio-inspired pheromone system for communication. Nano aerial robots, deployed in this study, act as agents and emit pheromone markers in an artificial environment upon detecting bouts. Leveraging the concept of artificial potential fields, the agents switch between exploiting the knowledge of the swarm by following pheromone gradients and exploring the search space by targeting a random point. The agents are repelled by each other and by walls to avoid collisions. The swarm GSL strategy is implemented into three nano aerial robots and validated in a real-world experiment in an indoor environment with a single gas source. The results indicate that the the swarm GSL strategy presented in this paper is capable of GSL in indoor environments and that the intermittency of gas distributions is a better source proximity indicator than the mean concentration.

articleTitle: Basic Characteristics of Optical Probe Current Sensor and Current Measurement Flowing through Bonding Wire of SiC Power Devices
abstract: The authors have developed an optical probe current sensor based on the Faraday effect of Bi:RIG crystals as a new current sensor that can replace conventional current sensors. This paper describes the measurement results of the basic characteristics of the developed current sensor and the actual in-situ measurement results of a bonding wire part of a SiC power semiconductor with a diameter of 300 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>.

articleTitle: An Electrochemical Microneedle Biosensor with Wide Linear Range for Continuous Glucose Monitoring
abstract: Wearable microneedle-based glucose sensor is a highly promising device for long-term continuous glucose monitoring. In particular, it is essential to develop minimally invasive a glucose sensor with long lifetime, wide linear range, and low limit of detection by ensuring long-term enzyme stability and reducing biofouling. In this study, we present a fully integrated polymeric microneedle sensor system with wireless and in vivo testing for real-time sensing of glucose levels in interstitial fluid (ISF). The developed device is compatible with a customized mobile apps for data visualization and collection. The microneedle glucose sensor utilizes a sandwich-type enzyme immobilization technique, enhanced by a newly developed double-layer permselective membrane coating, resulting in an impressive wide linear range of 0-31.45 mM and a low limit of detection (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.8\ \mu\mathrm{M}$</tex>) for glucose monitoring, while effectively minimizing fouling in ISF. Furthermore, the performance of the developed microneedle glucose sensor was validated through clinical testing using a rabbit model. The results provide evidence of its reliability and effectiveness in accurately measuring glucose levels in ISF.

articleTitle: A Double-Level Interleaved Group Convolutional Network in the Frequency Domain for E-Nose Gas Recognition
abstract: Electronic noses (E-noses) have attracted much attention in academia and industry. In this study, a homemade E-nose system composed of 15 gas sensors is constructed, and a dataset for 10 kinds of industrial pollution gases is collected. In addition, a double-level interleaved group convolutional network in the frequency domain (DIGC-F) is proposed to identify pollution gases. DIGC-F first transforms the time-domain signal to the frequency domain, and then the low-frequency coefficients are intercepted as new features to reduce the data dimension. This reduces feature redundancy and filters out high-frequency noise. In addition, an attention module is introduced to measure the importance of data features from different dimensions and channels. Finally, sensor-level and channel-level interleaved convolutional networks are designed to achieve full information interaction at the double level. Experiments on an industrial pollution gas dataset show that DIGC-F has better classification performance than other advanced deep learning methods.

articleTitle: 2D SERS Gas Sensor for Visualization and Localization of the Odor Source
abstract: Microbial volatile organic compounds (MVOCs) could be detected and used to understand the metabolic state of microorganisms. The gas sensor developed using the Surface Enhanced Raman Scattering (SERS) technique possesses ultra-high sensitivity and excellent selectivity, which is suitable for detecting low-concentration and complex MVOCs. Here, an odor source is simulated as a microbial community, and a 2D SERS sensor array is utilized to visualize the odor spatial distribution and localize the odor source. The Raman spectra of the odor adsorbed onto the sensor surface are collected after scanning the sensor array. A heatmap image is obtained by using the intensities of the characteristic peaks from the acquired Raman spectra. Thus, the odor spatial distribution is presented, and the localization of the odor source is determined by the image.

articleTitle: Comparing Data Representation Techniques for Tactile Sensing in Classification Tasks
abstract: The present paper explores the importance of utilizing statistical and frequency-based data pre-processing techniques in tactile sensing for robotic applications. The study compares the performance of raw data-based classification with these techniques and highlights the limitations of previous studies that overlook their benefits. The paper also discusses multimodal tactile sensing and relevant literature on statistical and frequency-based data preprocessing techniques applied to time series data from sensors. The aim is to enhance tactile sensing systems' classification accuracy and robustness for more efficient and effective robotic applications.

articleTitle: A Predictive Point-of-Care Platform for Early Detection of Periodontal Disease
abstract: Periodontal disease, a major global health concern, often goes undiagnosed until advanced stages due to the lack of effective early screening methods. This paper introduces the development of a non-invasive, point-of-care (PoC) diagnostic platform for the early detection and monitoring of periodontal disease using saliva. The system consists of a reusable detector device and a biosensor chip with multiple electrodes for simultaneous analysis of key oral metabolites (lactate, pyruvate, succinate, and fumarate) from which diagnosis predictions can be made. The biosensor employs enzymatic reactions for selective metabolite detection, with results indicating near-linear responses across the physiological ranges. Despite the complexity of saliva, minimal cross-interference was observed, demonstrating the platform's potential for accurate early diagnosis. The adaptability of the design also promises possibilities for its use in detecting other oral and systemic conditions. Future work will focus on clinical validations and further development of the companion app for comprehensive disease monitoring and management.

articleTitle: Force-Sensing Intelligent Vise for Cutting Dynamics Monitoring in Machining
abstract: This work demonstrates the use of a 3-axis piezoelectric force sensor embedded vise for generating cutting force data during machining. In particular, a unique geometrical design is employed to house the bulk piezoelectric material (PZT) within the vise structure, which helps to prevent the clamping and cutting forces from adding up and potentially damaging the PZT sensors. The resulting vise sensor has a dynamic range of cutting force of up to 800 N, which is necessary for rough machining of most common materials such as medium-carbon steel. The cutting force sensing vise is also used to demonstrate the capability of measuring the dynamic cutting force during cutting process, from which the data are used to identify the occurrence of chatter. The vise with built-in sensors offers a practical solution for real manufacturing scenarios and various applications, such as cutting force and chatter monitoring.

articleTitle: Bayesian Filter-Based Ultrasonic Continuous Hand Gesture Recognition for Low-Resource Platform
abstract: This work proposes a Bayesian filter-based algorithm for ultrasonic continuous hand gesture recognition on low-resource platforms. By using the phased property of hand gestures, our method enables robust recognition for continuous gesture streams at low inference frequencies and without explicit detection. Experiments show that the proposed method achieves a 93.1% performance accuracy and a 99% intended rate on an embedded system supporting an inference frequency of only 5Hz.

articleTitle: Materials Design for High Performance of Metal Oxide Semiconductor Gas Sensors
abstract: Our group has been conducting research on gas sensors for approximately 60 years. In the past, we have reported several important material designs and demonstrated the effectiveness of integrating them for achieving high performance. In recent years, aiming for further improvement, we have proposed and demonstrated gas sensors that combine the usefulness of these material designs with MEMS-type sensors, achieving ultra-high sensitivity and super selectivity.

articleTitle: Towards Wearable-Based Lung Sound Intensity Assessment Leveraging Impedance Pneumography
abstract: Respiratory diseases are a leading cause of mortality. Lung sound (LS) intensity is an important auscultation component that relates to sound transmission and generation in health and disease. The assessment of LS intensity outside laboratory and clinical settings remains understudied due to its dependency on auscultation location, respiratory phase, and airflow rate. Simultaneous Impedance Pneumography (IP) and multi-channel LS measurement presents a unique opportunity to provide such context. In this study, we evaluated the feasibility of fusing IP and LS to quantify the relationship between airflow and LS amplitude, and the effectiveness of continuous flow-correction. Wearable-based IP and LS at three different locations were measured simultaneously with spirometer airflow signals on 10 healthy volunteers while performing breathing maneuvers. The relationship between calibrated IP peak inspiratory flow (PIF) and inspiratory LS amplitude features, with and without flow-correction, was evaluated with correlation analysis. Our results confirmed the well-established significant relationship between LS amplitude and airflow (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R^{2}\geq 0.93,\ p < 0.001$</tex>) and demonstrated the flow-correction effectiveness in the 0.5-2.8 L/s PIF range. As such, this work may pave the way for a wearable-based quantitative LS intensity assessment.

articleTitle: Performance of a Multiparametric Water Quality Sensor in a Small-Scale Water Distribution Network
abstract: Ensuring access to good quality water is crucial for sustainable development, particularly in developing nations. However, the lack of affordable and reliable solutions for monitoring water quality remains a significant challenge that the LOTUS sensor meets: it is a compact and versatile multiparametric sensor designed for real-time monitoring of chlorine, pH, temperature, and conductivity in potable water. The proposed solution features a cylinder-like structure, measuring 21 cm long and 3.5 cm in diameter. It integrates temperature sensors, conductivity sensors, and a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2 \mathrm{x}10$</tex> sensor array of multi-walled carbon nanotube (CNT) chemistors. The CNTs, arranged in random networks between interdigitated electrodes, can remain non-functionalized or be functionalized with a dedicated polymer to modulate their sensitivity. Six LOTUS sensors were tested in a 44m-long water loop under a flow rate of 0.3m/s and pressure of 1 bar to evaluate the system performance. To manage the high noise levels caused by strong electromagnetic interferences in the facility, particularly under flowing water conditions, a strong effort was put into data denoising techniques. After extensive denoising and calibration model optimization, temperature, conductivity, chlorine, and pH estimation were achieved with mean absolute error (MAE) as low as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.34^{\mathrm{o}}\mathrm{C}, 73.2\mu \mathrm{S}/\text{cm}, 0.13\text{mg}/\mathrm{L}$</tex> and 0.12 pH unit in flowing water (achieved on different sensors due to dataset limitations). Notably, the dataset also demonstrates the role of CNT functionalization in chemical sensing, with the selected polymer modulating the sensitivity to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{pH}$</tex> by 50%.

articleTitle: MIP Functionalized Love Wave Sensor for Detection of 4-AP Organic Compound in Turbid Solutions
abstract: In the quest to detect target bio-chemical molecules in turbid waters using Love Wave (LW) acoustic sensor, we performed pilot experiments with 4-(Aminomethyl) Pyridine (4-AP), an organic compound, in Deionized (DI) water and Formazine based turbid solutions. This article reports the results of Molecularly Imprinted Polymer (MIP) functionalized Love wave (LW) acoustic sensor response for the detection of various concentrations of 4-AP with a focus on electro-acoustic response mechanism in turbid liquids. The detection of a very small concentrations of 4-AP down to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−7</sup> ppm, both in DI water and Formazine based turbid solutions was achieved.

articleTitle: MOS Sensors Characterizing Gas Absorption Dynamics for Art Conservation
abstract: A setup and methodology for analyzing the absorption of hazardous gases using saturated salt solutions for art conservation purposes is introduced. Metal oxide semiconductor (MOS) gas sensors are employed to monitor the absorption process of possibly corrosive hazards like acetic acid by saturated salt solutions within the headspace of a 2 L glass bottle. The presented setup enables the performance evaluation of saturated salt solutions, like potassium carbonate, magnesium nitrate, and magnesium chloride as potential agents for climate and pollution control in art conservation applications. The proposed setup is scalable to showcases in museums. It was found that potassium carbonate is most effective in absorbing potential pollutants.

articleTitle: Evaluation of a Non-Coherent Ultra-Wideband Transceiver for Micropower Sensor Nodes
abstract: Spatial and contextual awareness has the potential to revolutionize sensor nodes, enabling spatially augmented data collection and location-based services. With its high bandwidth, superior energy efficiency, and precise time-of-flight measurements, ultra-wideband (UWB) technology emerges as an ideal solution for such devices. This paper presents an evaluation and comparison of a non-coherent UWB transceiver within the context of highly energy-constrained wireless sensing nodes and pervasive Internet of Things (IoT) devices. Experimental results highlight the unique properties of UWB transceivers, showcasing efficient data transfer ranging from 2 kbit /s to 7.2 Mbit /s while reaching an energy consumption of 0.29 nJ /bit and 1.39 nJ /bit for transmitting and receiving, respectively. Notably, a ranging accuracy of up to ±25 cm can be achieved. Moreover, the peak power consumption of the UWB transceiver is with 6.7 mW in TX and 23 mW in RX significantly lower than that of other commercial UWB transceivers.

articleTitle: Resonance Frequency and Vibration Mode Modification of Piezoelectric MEMS Ultrasonic Sensors on Buckled Diaphragm Structures for High Sensitivity and High Resolution Measurement
abstract: Vibration modes and resonance frequencies of piezoelectric MEMS ultrasonic sensors with buckled diaphragm structures were investigated from the viewpoint of high resolution and ghost-suppressive measurement techniques using multiple frequencies. The resonance frequency was modified through inverse piezoelectric stress, and the buckling introduced to improve sensitivity also varied with the stress. The inverse piezoelectric stress was generated by applying an external voltage to the tuning electrode of the sensor in the range of 0 V to 10 V. The buckling deflection was accordingly varied from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{12}\ \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{6}\ \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}$</tex>, and the resonance frequency was varied in the range between 37 kHz and 102 kHz. As the result of the stress control, a multiple frequency technique that effectively improves the directivity and the resolution was achieved by combining 84 kHz and 37 kHz frequencies with tuning voltages of 0 V and 8 V, respectively. The buckling profiles and vibration modes of the sensor diaphragm at these tuning voltages were also well suitable for high-sensitivity measurements.

articleTitle: Preparation of PVP Encapsulated Pd:WO3 Nanocomposites for H2 Gas Sensing
abstract: This paper reports on the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}_{2}$</tex> gas sensing technique which has great importance in various practical applications. One of the current challenges lies in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}_{2}$</tex> gas sensing technique is a high-temperature operation that increases explosion risk. To this objective, the room temperature chemochromic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}_{2}$</tex> sensing technique is an alternative, yet the development is not explored widely. We developed a novel quasi-reversible <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}_{2}$</tex> sensing nanocomposite using an optimized ratio of Pd, WO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, and polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP). It provides rapid eye-readable chemochromic response with a long recovery time for multiple repeated cycles, which has potential importance in industrial monitoring.

articleTitle: A 36% Scandium Aluminum Nitride pMUT - FBAR Dual Mode Pressure Sensor for IoT Applications
abstract: This work presents a novel dual-mode frequency-based pressure sensor, which implements a Piezoelectric Mi-cromachined Ultrasonic Transducer (pMUT) operating in the fundamental flexural mode around 1.4 MHz and in the S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>bulk mode around 4.2 GHz. The sensor's active layer is fabricated with Scandium-doped Aluminum Nitride (ScAIN) thin film, with a doping level of 36%. The device's behavior is monitored under different temperature and pressure conditions by observing the resonance positions when excited at the respective modes. The sensor displays a change in the resonance frequency of the flexural mode and in the anti-resonance of the S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>bulk mode, with a shift of 3.5 kHz at 1.4 MHz (0.25%) and 8 MHz at 3.6 GHz (0.22%), respectively. This shift is observed over a pressure range spanning from 1 mbar to 1 bar. Furthermore, when the temperature range is varied from 20°C to 200°C, the anti-resonance of the S1 bulk mode is monitored, resulting in the estimation of the first and second order temperature coefficients of frequency (TCFs) as -40 ppm/K and -110 ppb/K<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, respectively.

articleTitle: Design of a Novel Tridimensional Silicon MEMS ThermoElectric Generator
abstract: A novel design of a MEMS ThermoElectric Generator (TEG) with a tridimensional structure manufactured with standard silicon-based processes is presented. The proposed 5 mm × 5 mm TEG embeds 221 cells connected electrically in parallel each composed of the electrical series of 15 pn-polysilicon-based thermocouples. Heat can be transferred from a hot side at temperature <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T$</tex> <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">H</inf> to a cold side at temperature Tc by means of high-thermal-conductivity copper paths immersed in low-thermal-conductivity resin mold that composes the package. The working principle has been validated through 3D finite-element simulations. An in-process test structure has been experimentally tested. An output voltage <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{V}_{\mathbf{TEG}}$</tex> of -3.3 mV has been measured for a temperature difference <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta \mathbf{T} =T_{\mathbf{H}}-T\mathbf{c}$</tex> of 6 °C, resulting in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\mathbf{TEG}} / \Delta \mathrm{T}=-550 \mu \mathbf{V} /{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$</tex> The final TEG device is expected to have an enhanced thermoelectric conversion efficiency due to the molding injection which will optimize the temperature difference across the thermocouples minimizing thermal leakage.

articleTitle: Thermally Driven Sol-Gel Transition of Gelatin in a 3D-Printed Microfluidic Chip
abstract: Here we show a facile microfluidic technique to cover an inner wall of microchannel with a thin film of gelatin hydrogel. This was implemented by embedding a temperature-controlling unit in a flow focusing microchannel device, which was fabricated using a 3D-printing method. By tuning the ratio of flow rates between water (gelatin) and oil, in situ sol-to-gel transition of gelatin flow in the locally cooled chip enabled us to selectively achieve symmetric or asymmetric gel coating of a rectangular channel surface in an efficient way.

articleTitle: ModAu: Modernized Auscultation
abstract: This paper presents a novel wireless digital stetho-scope design that integrates multiple sensing modalities into a compact form factor. The proposed stethoscope aims to enhance the auscultation data quality by capturing high-quality audio and precise vibration data for improved diagnosis and monitoring of respiratory and cardiac conditions. To enable wireless connectivity, the auscultation device incorporates the latest Bluetooth technology, enabling realtime transmission of auscultation data to a compatible device, such as a smartphone or computer. This allows future healthcare professionals to visualize and analyze the captured data using dedicated software, providing enhanced visualization tools, signal processing algorithms, and machine learning techniques for accurate interpretation and diagnosis. The compact form factor and low-cost design of the stethoscope, makes it suitable for various medical applications, including remote healthcare and long term monitoring.

articleTitle: Optical Fiber Coiled Sensors for Acoustic Oblique Wave Detection using Distributed Acoustic Sensing
abstract: Distributed Acoustic Sensors (DAS) are able to measure dynamic strain and temperature signals quantitatively along several kilometers of optical fiber using the properties of backscattering light. A drawback of DAS is the sensing resolution of around 1 meter long. This paper analyses the use of DAS as a vibration sensor for a thin plate structure using an acoustic excitation. A coiled method of arranging the sensing optical fibers enhances the measured signal and using a calibration method, the strain in the sensed region is obtained. The method can be used to characterize structures acoustically allowing the structure to detect the direction and reconstruct nearby acoustic events. Acoustic excitations were performed using a speaker at 1 meter distance to a 1 millimeter thick free-free 40 centimeters by 73 centimeter instrumented stainless steel plate inside an anechoic chamber. Results measured using reference microphones and accelerometers were compared to the optical fiber sensor through a Finite Element Model. The results demonstrate that the optical fiber system is able to measure the frequency response with an average 54 dB sound pressure level sound source chirp signal for flexural modes with a clear differentiation between angles of incidence up to 500 Hz.

articleTitle: Alleviating Slot Collisions in UHF RFID Systems
abstract: One of the main obstacles for low latency bulk reading in UHF RFID systems is collision occurrence. State-of-the-art high-speed identification methods mostly rely on collision recovery techniques or collision avoidance algorithms. Collision recovery can be done by enhancing the physical layer capabilities to support this feature. Usually, the probability of collision occurrence can be reduced by carefully optimizing the frame length and accurately estimating the number of tags in the interrogation area. In this paper, bulk reading time is reduced by detecting collisions in tag replies. More precisely, the RFID reader identifies slot types using the tag replies spectrum and the deviation in tag data rates which is known as rate tolerance. This novel reader feature distinguishes two types of collided slots; identified collided slots with shorter duration as compared to the non-identified ones. Hence, our technique drastically improves RFID tag reading times. Our experimental results show that the proposed technique can reduce bulk reading times by 10% compared to conventional receivers at SNR greater than 20dB.

articleTitle: Pristine, Au and Cu Decorated Nanoporous NiO Films for Selective CO and NO2 Gas Sensing
abstract: We report on a one-step, on-chip fabrication process of high-quality nanoporous p-type NiO thin films for gas sensing application. Highly nanoporous and polycrystalline NiO thin films were fabricated and deposited onto alumina substrates employing advanced gas deposition (AGD) technique. AGD-fabricated NiO films were further decorated with gold (AuNP) and copper (CuNP) nanoparticles, respectively. The nano-sensors array thus fabricated were integrated into a purpose-built hybrid senor unit that allows for in-situ conditioning and gas sensing measurement of volatile gases. The results revealed that the relative sensor responses of pure NiO towards CO gas exposures (reducing gas), were higher than the corresponding NP decorated NiO films. In contrast, AuNP decorated NiO sensors exhibited relatively higher sensor response towards oxidizing gases, NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, than CuNP decorated and pure NiO based nano-sensors. It is noted that the relative sensor response changes are mainly governed by the high porosity of the as-fabricated NiO films and the corresponding grain-grain Schottky barriers. Limits of detection (LOD) was estimated to be 1.5 ppm for CO and 400 ppb for NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> for pure and AuNP decorated NiO based sensors, respectively. The results are promising for further development of nanoporous p-type metal oxide sensors for specific volatile biomarkers detection, for example, in exhaled breath analysis for disease diagnosis.

articleTitle: Biological Sensor Based on Silicon Nanowires for Electrical Detection of Staphylococcus Aureus Bacteria
abstract: Biological sensor for bacteria (Staphylococcus aureus) detection was fabricated using silicon nanowires as sensitive units, with a two-level masking manufacturing process with conventional silicon microelectronics technologies. A chemical functionalization step was then used to attach the antibodies and bacteria. The sensor was made of two interdigited comb electrodes connected by silicon nanowires. The very large number of interlaced and functionalized silicon nanowires facilitated the attachment of biomolecules allowing an increased sensitivity to the detection of bacteria. This work used an approach that directly measured the electrical contribution of bacteria immobilised on the nanowires between two electrodes by a significant variation in current. The sensor showed a linear behaviour in the bacteria concentration 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup> CFU/mL and a sensitivity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$73\mu\mathrm{A}$</tex> per decade of CFU/mL.

articleTitle: E-Nose System Based on Ultra-Low Power Single Micro-LED Gas Sensor and Deep Learning
abstract: Electronic nose (e-nose) technology utilizing chemoresistive sensors has gained substantial attention across various domains such as smart factory and personal health monitoring. The primary challenge associated with chemoresistive sensors lies in their susceptibility to cross-reactivity towards different gas species. To address this issue, we propose an innovative approach based on a photoactivated gas sensor integrated with micro-LED. By applying a pseudorandom voltage input to the LED, transient sensor responses for various gases are induced. Subsequently, we employ a deep learning to analyze the complex transient signals obtained, facilitating prediction of gas species and concentrations. In particular, the proposed e-nose system achieves high accuracy of gas type determination and concentration prediction for various target gases with only 0.5 mW by using only single sensor. Since it consumes less than one hundredth of the power of the existing e-nose systems, it has the advantage of being able to operate for a long time in battery-powered situation, and this advantage is expected to be utilized in combination with internet-of-things (IoT) technologies.

articleTitle: Increasing Sensitivity of Mass Detection Using Nonlinear Micro/Nano-Mechanical Resonators
abstract: The contribution discusses possible approach(es) for detection of the mass of a (nano)particle/molecule attached to a micro/nano-mechanical resonator operating in non-linear vibrational conditions. The mass of the particle can be extracted either based upon the jump down/up frequencies or jump down/up amplitudes occurring upon the sweep over the first and/or second natural frequency of the resonator. To unambiguously identify the attached particle/molecule on the resonator, always two parameters are essential to be measured simultaneously. Either the two (consecutive) jump down/up frequencies in non-linear regime or just the first jump down/up frequency and corresponding maximal amplitude at the same moment. The last possibility is to combine both cases leading yet to a higher sensitivity of the mass detection. The mentioned approaches have their advantages and disadvantages which are described and discusses in this contribution.

articleTitle: A Direct Piezoresistive Method to Transduce Electromechanical Motion in Self-Sensing Suspended NanoStructures
abstract: We present a facile method to transduce nanome-chanical vibrations induced by electrostatic actuation in sus-pended nanostructures using their intrinsic piezoresistivity. The capacitive method largely used for graphene nanomechanical res-onators is not very effective for materials with lower conductivity and also for low dimensional structures. A piezoresistive method, however, can address the transduction of a wide range of mate-rials and nanostructures. We, in this effort, have formulated a piezoresistive transduction method that involves simple circuitry and has a non-scaling electrical background independent of the mechanical motion, unlike capacitive transduction schemes where the electrical background scales with the mechanical vibrational amplitude. This facilitates an easy discernment of the electrome-chanical resonance for different drive voltages. Experimental measurements performed on an in-house fabricated reduced graphene oxide (rGO)-based suspended piezoresistive membrane reliably support the formulation of the principle of piezoresistive transduction advanced in this paper.

articleTitle: Extract Spatial Distribution of a Specific Gas from Mixed Gas Data Measured by the LSPR Gas Sensor
abstract: Visualizing invisible gas molecules can be a great help to our lives. At present, gas sensors can already visualize the spatial distribution of gas mixture, however, the visualization of a specific gas requires further analysis of the measurement data. In this study, matrix decomposition is used to analyze the measurement data of localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) gas sensor. To satisfy the linear relationship between the concentration of gas and the output of the device required for applying matrix decomposition, we formulated a procedure for processing the measurement data instead of using them directly. To obtain the diffusion trace of a specific gas, we designed a method to obtain the characteristic output of the specific gas, then by using the characteristic output as the known information, the corresponding diffusion trace can be estimated better through the matrix decomposition algorithm. We used the designed method to analyze the measurement data, and the results show that our method can obtain the spatial distribution of some gas.

articleTitle: Ultra-Low Power MEMS Inertial Switch Based Wake-Up Wireless Sensing Node for Door Lock Monitoring
abstract: We present the first demonstration of our event-driven ultra-low power MEMS inertial switch for dry cabinet door lock monitoring. The MEMS inertial switch is integrated into a wireless sensing node (WSN) which houses a commercial accelerometer (ADXL355) and Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) module to detect the door lock status. Upon the acceleration generated by unlocking of the dry cabinet, the MEMS inertial switch is turned on and wakes up the BLE module and the accelerometer sequentially. After wake-up, the BLE module streams the accelerometer data to a remote PC tracking the activities on the dry cabinet door. The inertial switch successfully detects the door unlock events and wakes up the WSN to stream the accelerometer data for 2 hours. The data signature of the accelerometer is able to classify the status of the opening, closure and locking of door.

articleTitle: Application of a Photoacoustic Sensor for Colon Cancer Imaging: A Case Report
abstract: The incidence of colorectal cancer is on the rise on a global scale. Besides research into novel treatment schemes, accurate monitoring techniques are necessary to help in the process, especially for the post-treatment period. Recently, photoacoustic (PA) imaging has been investigated as a tool for detecting and monitoring colon cancer, with a potential of distinguishing various tissue types. In this initial study, we report using an LED-based PA sensor on a colon cancer specimen, ex-vivo. Our initial data with an LED of a wavelength equal to 850 nm shows that the PA signal is weaker in the malignant region when compared to healthy colon tissue or fat, while stronger than the signal in water (noise level). These results pave the way for larger studies, including data from more patients and various types of tumors.

articleTitle: LiDAR-Based Occupancy Grid Map Estimation Exploiting Spatial Sparsity
abstract: The problem of estimating occupancy grids to support automotive driving applications using LiDAR sensor point clouds is considered. We formulate the problem as a sparse binary occupancy value reconstruction problem. Our proposed occupancy grid estimation method is based on pattern-coupled sparse Bayesian learning and exploits the inherent sparsity and spatial occupancy dependencies in LiDAR sensor measurements. The proposed method demonstrates enhanced detection capabilities compared to commonly used benchmark methods, as observed through testing on scenes from the nuScenes dataset.

articleTitle: Advancing Transdermal Therapeutics: In-Vivo Assessment and Computational Insights into Porous Microneedle-Based Drug Delivery
abstract: Porous microneedles (MN) offer the advantage of allowing for higher dosage delivery because of their larger surface area and broader diffusion spread compared to topical delivery. In this study, porous MNs were fabricated using two-photon polymerization. We simulated the diffusion of fluorescein isothiocyanate (FITC)-dextran as a pseudo drug through the skin with and without the porous MN and proved that at a depth of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{100}\ \boldsymbol{\mu}\mathbf{m}$</tex> in the dermis, the porous MN delivers over 4 times the concentration of FITC-dextran compared to topical delivery. We also performed an in vivo study on mouse skin by delivering a fast green FCF stain through a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{5\times 5}$</tex> array of porous MNs. The dye was successfully delivered, and the array remained intact after insertion.

articleTitle: Dielectrophoretic Particle Focusing Using Axisymmetric Quadric Electrodes
abstract: To achieve the high-resolution separation of particles in size, focusing particles into a single stream in the centerline of a microchannel is required. Inertial microfluidic focusing may not be effective for particles smaller than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim \boldsymbol{3\ \mu} \mathbf{m}$</tex>. In this study, we used negative dielectrophoretic (nDEP) force generated by axisymmetric quadric electrodes to focus particles smaller than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{3\ \mu} \mathbf{m}$</tex> into a single stream. This requires fabrication of electrodes on both the top and the bottom surfaces of the microchannel. Unlike the device containing electrodes in one side of the channel, the device with axisymmetric electrodes poses much more complexity in its fabrication. This paper reports a simple and cost-effective fabrication method. Fluorescent polystyrene particles of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{2\ \mu} \mathbf{m}$</tex> diameter were successfully focused in the centerline of the microchannels with two different types of electrodes - chromium (Cr) and indium tin oxide (ITO). We also investigated frequency effects on direction of DEP force and the particles alignment.

articleTitle: Live Demonstration: IoT based smart vertical farming framework with sensor network and mobile application for real-time monitoring
abstract: FarmTech is an affordable and automated vertical farming setup for high-yield indoor cultivation in small spaces. Its features include a vertically stacked lightweight structure with integrated LEDs for providing energy to the crop for photosynthesis. It has an energy-efficient sensor network connected with Wi-Fi for monitoring and communication of live data from the farm to an IoT platform Thingspeak. An automated irrigation system utilizes data from soil moisture sensors. FarmView mobile app enables remote access to live farm updates and warnings from Thingspeak data.

articleTitle: Comprehensive LiDAR Sensor Noise Model and Application to Texture and Object Classification using Custom Deep Learning
abstract: This paper presents a new approach that involves (1) proposing a comprehensive noise model using automotive Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) sensor data and (2) applying the model in object classification based on the texture difference of the objects. We first generated our own sensor data from a 16-channel Velodyne LiDAR to measure several objects with different textures. Then, we selected suitable deep learning techniques, with a particular emphasis on data that were not thoroughly considered in conventional analyses, to extract detailed information about intricate textures on the surfaces of different objects. The proposed technique classifies the texture, which in turn facilitates object classification. We tested and validated the proposed method through custom experiments to demonstrate its performance in classifying objects with different textures. The model achieved a high accuracy exceeding 99%, suggesting that our approach has the potential to be applied to classification tasks such as object recognition and segmentation.

articleTitle: Effects of Various Head Movement Executions on Spatial Accuracy of Magnetoencephalography Systems
abstract: Head movements during magnetoencephalography (MEG) recordings lead to a smearing of the magnetic field distribution measured by the MEG sensors and thus to a significant degradation of the MEG spatial accuracy. This in turn is associated with inaccurate source localization. Head movement detection was applied to MEG recordings performed under the condition of different degrees of head movement (moderate, weak, quasi-no) and compared with individually constructed head-cast recordings. The center of the head moved on average around 4.8 mm for moderate motion and 3.5 mm for weak motion. Even without movement execution, the head center moved around 1.4 mm on average, which could be significantly minimized to less than 0.2 mm by using an individual head-cast. In addition, it was found that repositioning of the head within the MEG scanner could be realized with a mean deviation of the MEG sensor positions of around 1 mm with the use of an individual head-cast, while this deviation was around 4.7 mm without head-cast. Our work suggests that the use of head-casts allows maximization of the spatial precision of MEG systems and ensures the comparability of separately recorded sessions.

articleTitle: Advancing Urban Air Quality Monitoring: A Hybrid Mobile-Stationary Approach
abstract: This paper presents a modular and mobile environmental monitoring system that integrates an array of sensors to monitor various environmental parameters. The system offers flexibility through its modular design, allowing for the integration of sensors based on specific monitoring requirements. This waterproof system is equipped with sensors, a solar power source, and a cellular module for data transmission and Global Positioning System (GPS) tracking. Real-time data visualization and an alert system are provided through a user-friendly dashboard. Field evaluation demonstrates the system's resilience in harsh conditions and its ability to provide accurate and reliable environmental data. This work contributes to the advancement of environmental monitoring technologies and offers a cost-effective solution for assessing and managing environmental conditions.

articleTitle: CRISPR-Based Diagnostic for In-Field Detection of Plant Pathogens
abstract: Plant fungal pathogens are an increasingly common and costly threat to agricultural yields, resulting in wasted produce and the frequent use of fungicides. To enable more targeted use of fungicides, methods for detecting and identifying plant fungal infections in a rapid, low-cost, decentralized, and power-free manner are needed. CRISPR-based diagnostics have recently emerged as an effective tool for sensitive and specific pathogen detection in resource-limited settings. We present the preliminary designs of a CRISPR-based diagnostic for the soil-borne fungus Colletotrichum coccodes. Bioinformatics analysis led to the identification of four gRNA candidates targeting the ITS 1 and ITS 2 regions of C. coccodes for high specificity. The most promising gRNA was further screened and detection of DNA concentrations down to 500 pM without amplification are shown. This diagnostic for C. coccodes could be used in agricultural settings for rapid and cost-effective detection of fungal pathogens to enable high-yield sustainable agricultural practices.

articleTitle: Bioimpedance as a Signature for Characterizing Human Ventricular Myocardium
abstract: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) continue to be a significant global burden in their prevalence and impact on public health. An experimental system incorporating a microchip with interdigitated electrodes (IDEs) and a microheater is developed for quantifying the electrical properties of the myocardial tissues excised from the healthy controls (cadaver bodies), rheumatic heart disease (RHD), and myxomatous valve disease (MVD) patients. Measuring bioimpedance at 25°C and 37°C can distinguish normal from fibrotic heart tissues. The impedance of normal tissue was significantly lower than fibrotic myocardial tissue <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{p} < =1.4\mathrm{e}-3$</tex> (at 25°C) and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{p} < =1\mathrm{e}-4$</tex> (at 37°C)). Based on these initial findings, we envisage measuring bioimpedance using a microchip on a larger cohort to distinguish normal from fibrotic myocardial tissues.

articleTitle: A Metal Nanoparticles and 2D-Siloxene Sheets Incorporated Laser-Ablated Graphene-Based Epidermal Patch for Electrolytes Analysis and Monitoring
abstract: For the unobtrusive monitoring of sodium and potassium ions, an electrochemical epidermal patch based on Au nanoparticles and a siloxene-functionalized laser-ablated graphene electrode has been developed. The siloxene sheets coated on the working electrodes significantly increase the contact area due to their laminar structure. Furthermore, the electrodeposited Au nanoparticles further increase the overall surface area of the solid contact material resulting in enhanced electric double-layer capacitance at the interface between the ion-selective membranes and solid-state contacts, thereby facilitating ion-to-electron transduction by its' inherent excellent electrical conductivity, ultimately leading to improved sodium and potassium ion detection stability with a Nernstian sensitivity of 59.667 and 58.490 mV/decade for Na<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> and K<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> towards wide concentration ranges of 0.5-636.5 mM and 0.1-156.6 mM respectively. Ion-selective sensors have also been effectively used in both artificial and human sweat.
